Contextual Dataset adapter/open, Arrow predicates and IO framing establish local calls only; full Dataset/backend lifecycle remains pending. Source-derived partial-write, overflow, parent-validity and repeated-finish risks were not runtime-reproduced. Preserve frozen legacy behavior and implement new capabilities in current-format paths (AGENTS.md:13-18).
ranges: SPDX header, private statistics child module and imports. Arrow arrays/builders/ArrayData support recursive writes and offset construction; async_recursion boxes recursion and async_trait implements the static manifest hook. Lance Schema/error, ObjectStore/Writer, legacy codecs/page tables/metadata and shared FileWriteSummary form the boundaries. No modern encoder, current-version strategy or feature/environment lookup is present.

Public async_trait ManifestProvider declares static async store_schema(&mut dyn Writer,&Schema)->Result<Option<usize>>. It separates file storage from the table manifest type; docs require dictionaries already persisted and their schema offsets/lengths populated. The provider returns an optional position but this trait does not validate it or specify atomicity/cleanup. The documented table implementation uses a schema-only V1 Manifest and writes it through do_write_manifest, avoiding a second dictionary write (rust/lance-table/src/io/manifest.rs:232-250).

Test-only pub(crate) empty NotSelfDescribing implements ManifestProvider and immediately returns Ok(None), without writing bytes. It is not a production export. Footer metadata serializes absence as zero through the existing metadata conversion; the reader requires an externally supplied schema in these fixtures.

Public generic FileWriter requires M:ManifestProvider+Send+Sync and owns public Box<dyn Writer>, private Schema, signed next batch_id, PageTable, Metadata, optional StatisticsCollector and PhantomData<M>. The marker carries provider type without constructing provider state. No custom Drop, abort guard, closed flag or ownership-consuming finish exists. Replacing/writing the public object_writer can desynchronize existing tables/metadata. The ignored documentation example uses obsolete new/write(single batch)/shutdown syntax and missing awaits; actual API is try_new/write(slice)/finish.

Public FileWriterOptions derives Debug/Clone/Default and has only collect_stats_for_fields:Option<Vec<i32>>. Default None requests all schema IDs that support statistics; Some(empty) disables the collector. Some(nonempty) is projected with include_all_children=true in the constructor, so requesting a struct parent can include descendants. No size/version/compression option or explicit unknown/duplicate/negative-ID validation exists here.

Public async try_new creates the target writer before constructing Self. It owns the supplied Schema and borrows options. Store creation errors propagate; any later panic/construction failure has no local delete/abort handling. Publication, overwrite policy and backend durability belong to ObjectStore/Writer implementations, not this call.

with_object_writer clones explicit stats IDs or obtains every schema field ID; nonempty IDs project a stats schema including descendants, then StatisticsCollector::try_new may still return None if no supported field exists. Empty IDs bypass projection/collector. It initializes next batch0 and default page table/metadata and retains schema/writer. No schema validation, dictionary hydration, counter limit or writer-position check occurs. Collector creation is Option, not a Result error (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/statistics.rs:586-629); this local body always returns Ok after successful construction.

schema returns a borrowed stored Schema. Private recursive verify_field_nullability rejects arr.null_count()>0 only when the corresponding stored Field is nonnullable, returning InvalidInput naming the field. It zips schema children with ArrayData child_data and recurses without applying an ancestor validity mask, slicing logical list children, checking child counts, or qualifying the name with ancestors. Extra children on either side are ignored by zip locally; earlier schema compatibility and Arrow construction supply other constraints.

verify_nullability_constraints zips top-level batch columns and stored fields by position, converts each array to ArrayData, and propagates the first recursive nullability failure. It does not itself compare field count, name, type or order; public write performs schema compatibility first.

write takes a slice of RecordBatch and returns success immediately for an empty slice: no schema validation, stats, bytes, flush or batch-ID change. Otherwise it validates every batch before mutating writer state: Arrow-to-Lance Schema conversion, check_compatible using default options except Ignore nullability, then actual stored-field null checks. Defaults ignore metadata, dictionary contents and field IDs, but require normal ordered field/name/logical-type compatibility; blob logical comparison retains its shared-child exception (rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/field.rs:83-103; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/field.rs:423-440; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:930-980). The comment assumes dictionary compatibility was checked elsewhere; this function neither checks nor unifies values.

If a collector exists, fields_in_batches traverses scalar leaves of structs and appends one statistics row per matching field ID for the entire supplied slice. Statistics are mutated before any page writes and are not rolled back on later errors/cancellation. No stats row is collected for list descendants or other nested fields. Unsupported/missing builders are skipped; collection executes synchronously within the async write future.

Clone top-level fields to avoid self borrowing, then process fields sequentially in schema order. For each field, resolve every batch column by name and collect borrowed ArrayRefs, with InvalidInput on a missing name. Call recursive write_array with the current batch_id and shared mutable page table; all supplied batches become one stored batch. There is no task spawn, field-level concurrency, transaction or rollback: earlier bytes/page entries/stats survive a later field error.

After all fields succeed, cast each input row count to i32, sum unchecked, and push cumulative Metadata length. Flush underlying AsyncWrite before returning so in-flight requests keep being polled and do not time out while caller waits. Increment batch_id only after flush succeeds. A flush failure can therefore leave page entries/stats and cumulative row metadata advanced with batch_id unchanged; retry is not locally safe/idempotent. Casts, sums, cumulative offsets and batch increment have no checked overflow handling. Flush is not final shutdown/publication.

add_metadata inserts owned key/value strings into stored schema metadata, replacing duplicate keys. finish_with_metadata clones/extends every provided entry (caller entries win), then invokes finish. Neither enforces a before-finish state, validates reserved keys, changes data pages, or restores metadata on finalization failure.

finish borrows self mutably, writes footer, then explicitly calls Writer::shutdown on the inner writer. Its authoritative size comes from shutdown WriteResult, not tell after shutdown; it discards other WriteResult identity metadata. Row count is last signed cumulative offset or0, cast to u64. No closed marker, repeated-finish guard, automatic abort/delete, idempotent retry or Drop finalization is provided. A footer error skips shutdown; shutdown error returns failure after footer mutation/writes.

len delegates Metadata::len (last cumulative offset cast to usize); is_empty is len()==0 and may be true after a zero-row stored batch. tell forwards the mutable underlying Writer cursor/error, not a durability guarantee. next_batch_id returns signed counter incremented only after successful flush. These accessors do not establish a finished state or validate overflows.

Private boxed-recursive write_array asserts a nonempty array slice, dispatches on the first actual array DataType and collects dyn Array references. Null routes to payload-free page metadata, fixed-stride types to Plain, then binary-like types to VarBinary. The Arrow predicate includes Utf8View/BinaryView while BinaryEncoder supports only the four offset-based types; reaching that adapter with views is not implicit conversion (rust/lance-arrow/src/lib.rs:99-137; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:91-105). No mixed-array type preflight is local.

Dictionary dispatch writes keys using the first array key type. Struct converts every array through the asserting cast helper then recursively writes child fields. Explicit FixedSizeList/FixedSizeBinary branches duplicate the earlier fixed-stride predicate and are not reached for those types under the current predicate; they do not provide broader element support.

List and LargeList route to respective i32/i64 offset writers; unmatched types return Schema error naming the actual type. This differs from reader unsupported-type panic. Dispatch is based on actual array type, with encoding tags asserted later in adapters; no compression strategy or version choice is negotiated here.

write_null_array sums lengths through i32 casts, awaits tell and records PageInfo at current position with logical row count, then returns. It writes no payload and does not inspect field.encoding or validity. Position may be shared with another page; table entry is enough for Null reconstruction. No checked count conversion.

write_fixed_stride_array asserts field.encoding==Some(Plain) and nonempty arrays, then PlainEncoder using first actual DataType. Only after encode success does it sum i32 logical row lengths and set/overwrite (field.id,batch_id) PageInfo with returned offset. The length is elements, not bytes; encoding failure may already have written bytes without a page entry. No separate validity buffer is written by this adapter.

write_binary_array asserts VarBinary, invokes BinaryEncoder and records returned position plus summed i32 logical element count. Binary returned position points to absolute i64 offsets after value bytes, not the beginning of payload. This wrapper performs no validity write, mixed-type check, row limit check or rollback.

write_dictionary_arr asserts Dictionary, encodes keys only via DictionaryEncoder with supplied key DataType and stores key-byte offset plus logical key count. Dictionary values are not pulled from batches, compared, merged or stored here; footer uses the separate stored schema dictionaries. A missing or stale schema dictionary can therefore fail at finalization or disagree with already emitted keys.

write_struct_array asserts every StructArray has exactly field.children.len columns, then walks child schema order. Resolve each batch child by name, return Schema error with child name and actual struct DataType if absent, and recursively write collected child arrays sequentially. No parent page or struct-parent validity is persisted; child bytes can precede a later error. Async recursion boxes nested calls, without spawning tasks.

write_list_array allocates an i32 positions builder with capacity equal to total logical rows (although it appends rows+1 positions), a retained Vec of sliced child arrays and initial0. For every list, assert offsets nonempty; slice child values from first through final offset, normalize each subsequent offset by subtracting that list start and adding accumulated last_offset, then append via unchecked i32 casts. It ignores list validity and keeps every child value in the selected span, including storage behind null lists. Arithmetic and offset/index conversions are unchecked; sliced tails outside the selected span are not encoded.

Write normalized positions first through the Plain adapter using the list parent Field, so that parent page length is total list rows+1. Then gather retained child slices and recursively write children[0] at the same batch ID. Missing child panics at indexing; a child failure can leave parent position bytes/table entry. No separate list validity, child-name metadata rewrite or parent null mask is persisted.

write_large_list_array mirrors List with an Int64 positions builder and unchecked i64 casts, but uses usize start/end/accumulation internally. Initial0 plus normalized per-array offsets concatenate logical lists and selected child spans. No list validity or offset-overflow validation; builder capacity again omits the terminal extra slot.

LargeList writes the i64 parent positions page first, gathers retained values, then recursively writes the first schema child at the same batch ID. Its parent page length includes terminal offset. Error/cancellation after positions has no local undo; zero logical rows still have one position if the outer supplied batch slice is nonempty.

write_statistics mutably finishes the optional collector. A nonempty successful stats batch has a debug-only row-count equality with next_batch_id; convert its Arrow schema to fresh Lance Schema and call schema.field_ids for leaf_field_ids despite that accessor including all preorder IDs, including struct roots (rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:600-604). Write each stats root recursively at batch0 using a separate page table, then serialize that table from field ID0. Return schema, all IDs and table offset. Propagate collector/write errors; absent collector or zero stats rows yields None. Collector builders are finished before these writes, so a later failure does not preserve unconsumed stats for retry (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/statistics.rs:635-670).

write_footer first unwraps minimum ID across all stored schema fields, including parents, then serializes the ordinary page table and stores its position. Empty schema panics before page-table write; nonempty schema without any page entries gets the page-table empty InvalidInput (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/page_table.rs:94-113). Next write statistics and replace stats_metadata. No staging/footer commit marker or rollback is installed.

Footer then persists stored schema dictionary values, mutating offsets/lengths, calls static M::store_schema and records its optional position, writes framed Metadata, and emits metadata position plus shared major0/minor2/LANC tail. Provider offsets are trusted, and provider errors occur after previous data/table/stats/dictionary side effects. WriteExt framing is u32 LE size then protobuf; tail is i64 LE position, i16 LE major/minor and magic bytes (rust/lance-io/src/traits.rs:83-106; rust/lance-file/src/format.rs:30-33). No alignment padding or v2 footer is added here. End of generic implementation.

Private fields_in_batches requires a nonempty batch slice (indexes batches[0]) and initially pairs schema roots with per-position arrays across all batches using zip. It allocates a Vec of borrowed arrays per visited field; mismatched count/order is not checked locally. Public write validates first and returns early on empty input.

Iterator uses a LIFO work stack: roots are initially pushed in forward order, then popped in reverse; structs push children in forward order and likewise visit reverse. Struct nodes themselves are not emitted. Other nested types are skipped entirely, including their descendants; scalar leaves return field plus array references. Traversal does not combine ancestor null masks with child validity, and collection order differs from the collector BTreeMap output ordering.

Test-only module imports Arrow temporal/decimal/dictionary/nested arrays, timezone types, concat, Arc and the V1 FileReader. Seven active Tokio tests and local fixture helpers follow; no source test is executed by this knowledge-base analysis.

test_write_file builds a 19-root Arrow schema covering Null, Boolean, Int64, Float32, Utf8, Decimal128/256(7,3), four Duration units, UInt32-key UTF8 dictionary, FixedSizeList<Float32,16>, FixedSizeBinary8, List/LargeList<UTF8>, List/LargeList<dictionary>, and Struct<Int64,UTF8>. Nullability varies but no non-Null-type null entries are constructed later. The schema is explicitly supplied on read, so this is not self-describing discovery coverage.

Broad roundtrip fixture creates 100 dictionary values cycling a/b/c, a 1600-value Float32 buffer grouped16, 800 bytes all123 grouped8, and 100 two-element lists with 200 string/dictionary children for each offset width. Values are nonnull and list offsets start0; it does not exercise sliced/null lists or changed dictionaries across batches.

The 19 columns each have100 rows: Null length100; Boolean mod3; Int64/Float32 and decimal values0..99; decimal precision7/scale3; Duration values0..99; prepared dictionary/fixed/list arrays; and a struct whose Int64 child is100..199 and string child0..99. RecordBatch construction unwraps Arrow validation. These exact values/types form the equality oracle rather than a performance measurement.

Attach dictionary values into the Lance schema before constructing NotSelfDescribing memory writer; write one batch, finish, reopen with original hydrated schema and compare complete batch equality. No shutdown size, schema-only manifest, IO count, cancellation or failed-write assertion is made.

Dictionary-first-field fixture puts a UInt32/UTF8 dictionary in sole column d with100 cyclic a/b/c values, preloads schema dictionary, writes/finishes and reopens using that schema. Exact equality covers dictionary at field0, not remapping, evolving dictionary contents, null keys or dictionary hydration from file.

Temporal fixture writes two rows of TimestampSecond without timezone [11111111,22222222] and TimestampMicrosecond with America/Los_Angeles [3333333,4444444]. Reopen with supplied schema and assert whole-batch equality. It proves those metadata/unit/value combinations only, not timezone conversion or all temporal types.

Empty nonnullable UTF8 fixture writes a nonempty outer slice containing a zero-row RecordBatch, finishes, asserts summary.num_rows==0, reopens batch0 and asserts zero rows. It does not test write(&[]), finishing before any write, empty schema, size bytes or the number of stored batches. This differs from the empty-slice no-op.

Statistics fixture declares Int64 i/i2, List<Int32> l, and struct s(si:Int64,sb:UTF8), then explicitly selects IDs[0,1,5,6]. Its comments claim requested-only, struct traversal and list omission coverage, but no supported scalar is omitted from the request and the list itself is not requested; it does not isolate all those policies.

Assert two-row stats: null counts all0; minima [1,5],[4,10],[1,4],[a,d]; maxima [3,6],[6,11],[3,5],[c,e]. The linked FIXME says maxima should not be incremented, but actual expected UTF8 maxima equal observed maxima c/e; do not infer incremented output from that stale comment.

stats_schema helper creates one nonnullable Struct root named decimal field ID, with nonnullable Int64 null_count and nullable min_value/max_value using supplied DataType. It preserves caller field iteration order and supplies no root metadata.

Private test Stats stores field_id, null-count Vec and min/max ArrayRefs. stats_batch derives root types from minima, builds child fields matching stats_schema, clones count values and array Arcs, creates all-valid structs, then unwraps RecordBatch construction. It performs no independent max-type or length validation before Arrow constructors.

read_file_as_one_batch opens with supplied Schema, reads all stored batches sequentially, retains them all in Vec and concatenates using reader schema. Unwraps every step; this is a test convenience, not a streaming production path or memory bound.

Shared-buffer test slices one Int32 array0..1000 into250 four-row writes, finishes and asserts object size strictly below16000 bytes. Read all batches via helper and compare column i exactly to original array. This catches repeated whole-buffer storage for this scalar case; it does not assert exact file size, request count, memory usage, null handling or zero-copy execution.

Schema conversion, encoding IO adapter, exact dispatch, current-version composition/compression selection, shared structural projection, writer facade and type checks are covered. Exact current reader metadata/projection modules and V2_1/V2_2/V2_3 writer wrappers/shared pipeline are covered; V2_0 writer, testing utilities and compatibility test/generator sources are covered in the [V2_0/compatibility supplement](rust-lance-file-v20-compatibility.md). The [concat supplement](rust-lance-file-concat.md) covers complete-file assembly and Blob part validation. [Orientation](../L0-orientation.md) · [Table metadata](rust-lance-table.md) · [Format](../L3-symbols/format-spec.md) · [Scenarios](../L4-crosscutting/scenarios.md) · [Build/test](../L4-crosscutting/build-and-test.md)

# lance-file: file versions and entry points

**INCOMPLETE.** Forty-seven of 56 inventory entries are analyzed (22,782 physical text/symlink lines). Schema conversion, encoding IO adapter, exact dispatch, current-version composition/compression selection, shared structural projection, writer facade and type checks are covered. Exact current reader metadata/projection modules and V2_1/V2_2/V2_3 writer wrappers/shared pipeline are covered; V2_0 writer, testing utilities and compatibility test/generator sources are covered in the [V2_0/compatibility supplement](rust-lance-file-v20-compatibility.md). The complete [writer-test catalog](rust-lance-file-writer-tests.md) is also covered. The [shared reader](rust-lance-file-shared-reader.md) now covers full/indexed metadata loading, local caching, read dispatch and tests. The [concat supplement](rust-lance-file-concat.md) covers complete-file assembly and Blob part validation. The [V1 foundation supplement](rust-lance-file-v1-foundation.md) covers projection, dictionary dispatch, metadata and page tables; the [V1 concrete codec supplement](rust-lance-file-v1-codecs.md) covers binary/plain/dictionary implementations. The [full V1 reader](rust-lance-file-v1-reader.md) and [V1 writer](rust-lance-file-v1-writer.md) are covered; modern encoding/IO scheduler implementations, binary fixture payloads and benches remain pending. README describes an internal crate not intended for external use, despite public Rust modules. (rust/lance-file/README.md:1-6)

[Orientation](../L0-orientation.md) · [Table metadata](rust-lance-table.md) · [Format](../L3-symbols/format-spec.md) · [Scenarios](../L4-crosscutting/scenarios.md) · [Build/test](../L4-crosscutting/build-and-test.md)

## Responsibility and routes

The crate declares readers/writers for the Lance file format. Its facade exports concat,datatypes,format,reader,testing,version,versions,writer; io is crate-visible with LanceEncodingsIo publicly reexported; compatibility_tests is private under cfg(test). The [runtime-boundary supplement](rust-lance-file-runtime.md) covers schema conversion, IO adaptation, exact dispatch and writer interfaces; the [structural writer supplement](rust-lance-file-structural-writer.md) covers current structural writer lifecycles, and the [V2_0/compatibility supplement](rust-lance-file-v20-compatibility.md) covers the separate array writer and fixture harness. Shared reader loading/cache/projection orchestration is covered in the [shared reader supplement](rust-lance-file-shared-reader.md); V1 foundations and concrete binary/plain/dictionary codecs are covered separately; the [full V1 reader](rust-lance-file-v1-reader.md) is covered. Delegated modern encoding/IO scheduling remain pending. (rust/lance-file/README.md:3-6; rust/lance-file/src/lib.rs:4-17)

```text
lance_file
|-- version: request policy -> exact identity -> metadata/footer codecs
|-- determine_file_version: size -> last8 bytes -> magic -> exact identity
|-- format: generated pb / pbfile, LANC magic and legacy0.2 constants
|-- io: range splitting, empty placeholders and ordered reassembly
|-- datatypes: flat protobuf fields <-> core schema trees
|-- versions: exact dispatch, composition/policies, current reader grammar and all exact V2 writers
|   `-- v1: projection/dictionary dispatch/metadata/page table covered; concrete implementations pending
|-- writer: facade/options/type checks and shared structural pipeline covered
|-- reader: full/indexed metadata, cache, projections, read dispatch and tests covered
|-- concat: compatibility, Blob part gates, page relocation and output lifecycle
|-- testing: public local-file/cache helpers, collecting IO
`-- compatibility_tests: private cfg(test), pinned stable bytes / current unstable determinism
```

Routes follow rust/lance-file/src/lib.rs:4-60 and rust/lance-file/src/version.rs:19-262. No capability is inferred from numeric release order.

See [current composition and structural projection](rust-lance-file-composition.md) for ordered version policies and shared metadata contracts.

See [exact reader grammar](rust-lance-file-readers.md) for metadata validation order and version-specific acceptance.

## Caller requests and persisted identities

LanceFileVersion is a caller selector with Legacy,V2_0,V2_1,Stable,V2_2,Next,V2_3. Default is exact V2_2. resolve() maps Stable->V2_2,Next->V2_3 and exact variants to themselves (Legacy->V1). is_unstable is true only after resolving to V2_3. Display/serde preserve stable/next as strings; they are request serialization, not strict persisted identity codecs. (rust/lance-file/src/version.rs:19-127)

FromStr lowercases but does not trim. Accepted aliases are0.1/legacy,2.0/0.3,2.1,2.2,2.3,stable,next. ConcreteFileVersion has only V1,V2_0,V2_1,V2_2,V2_3, derives Hash but no ordering, and has no Default/serde/FromStr implementation here. Strict from_manifest_string accepts canonical0.1/2.0/2.1/2.2/2.3 only. to_selector always produces exact variants, losing prior policy intent. (rust/lance-file/src/version.rs:92-107; rust/lance-file/src/version.rs:128-197)

| Exact identity | Manifest string | DataFile metadata(u32,u32) | Standard footer(u16,u16) | Embedded footer(u16,u16) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| V1 |0.1 |(0,2) |(0,2) |(0,2) |
| V2_0 |2.0 |(2,0) |(0,3) |(2,0) |
| V2_1 |2.1 |(2,1) |(2,1) |(2,1) |
| V2_2 |2.2 |(2,2) |(2,2) |(2,2) |
| V2_3 |2.3 |(2,3) |(2,3) |(2,3) |

Both numeric decoders accept(0,0..=2) as V1 and(0,3)/(2,0) as V2_0, plus the other listed exact pairs. They reject everything else with InvalidInput Unknown Lance storage version: value. Strict string decoding rejects0.3 even though request parsing and numeric footer alias handling accept their respective historical forms. The table describes mapping functions, not proof every writer calls them. (rust/lance-file/src/version.rs:172-272)

## Footer detection and errors

determine_file_version takes ObjectStore,Path,optional known usize size. If unknown, await store.size and checked-convert; if known, trust it. Reject size<8, await open_with_size and get_range(size-8..size), require footer[4..]==LANC, decode first four bytes as LEu16 major/minor and dispatch exact parser. IO errors propagate; size/magic/version errors are InvalidInput. Fewer than4 returned bytes could panic because no explicit received-length check precedes slicing. (rust/lance-file/src/lib.rs:25-60; rust/lance-file/src/format.rs:30-33)

This reads only the final8 bytes and does not verify pages, schema, full footer structure or data validity. The local async fixture uses synthetic8-byte legacy footers with no data. Known size avoids the explicit size call, but underlying store.open behavior and total request count remain pending. (rust/lance-file/src/lib.rs:30-59; rust/lance-file/src/version.rs:411-430)

## Dependencies, features and build

Package metadata/toolchain/lints inherit workspace. Runtime dependencies declare Lance Arrow/core/encoding/IO, Arrow arithmetic/array/buffer/cast/data/schema/select, async-recursion/async-trait, byteorder/bytes, datafusion-common, futures/log/num-traits, object_store,prost/prost-types,serde,tokio,tracing. Exact dependency versions, transitive features and exhaustive use-site reasons remain pending root/dependency analysis; reviewed code uses core errors/deepsize, serde and store/path types. (rust/lance-file/Cargo.toml:1-40; rust/lance-file/src/version.rs:4-11; rust/lance-file/src/lib.rs:19-23)

Dev dependencies are lance-datagen,lance-testing,criterion,rstest,proptest,pretty_assertions,rand,test-log,libc. Build dependencies prost-build and optional protobuf-src support protoc feature. docs.rs requests that feature; its Ubuntu rationale is a source comment, not a live service check. Reader/schema benches disable the standard harness. (rust/lance-file/Cargo.toml:41-72)

build.rs optionally sets PROTOC through unsafe process-environment mutation, enables proto3 optional, maps .lance.encodings to lance_encoding::format::pb and compiles shared file/file2/encodings_v2_0/encodings_v2_1 schemas. The protos symlink targets ../../protos/. format::pb and pbfile include generated lance.file.rs and lance.file.v2.rs. No build/install was performed. (rust/lance-file/build.rs:1-29; rust/lance-file/protos:1-1; rust/lance-file/src/format.rs:4-28)

## Extension boundary

Keep caller selectors distinct from exact storage identities; a new exact version needs explicit string/data-metadata/standard-footer/embedded-footer mapping and explicit capabilities elsewhere. Do not infer support by ordering, persist Stable/Next in manifests, or collapse the v2.0 footer alias distinction. The local tests pin these mappings but do not establish full historical reader/writer compatibility. Exact reader/writer dispatch and shared type checks are now covered in the runtime-boundary supplement; all exact V2 writer mechanisms and compatibility test/generator sources are now covered. Shared reader orchestration and tests are covered; encoding byte algorithms, delegated IO/decoder scheduling, binary fixture payloads remain pending. (rust/lance-file/src/version.rs:29-50; rust/lance-file/src/version.rs:128-262; rust/lance-file/src/version.rs:291-430)

## Schema reconstruction and persistence conversion

Fields(pub Vec<pb::Field>) and FieldsWithMeta{fields:Fields,metadata:HashMap<String,Vec<u8>>} are public. From<&Field> recursively flattens parent then children; From<&Schema> concatenates root subtrees. They preserve supplied IDs/parent IDs and do not validate or assign them. TryFrom<&Fields> for Schema reconstructs iteratively and supplies empty schema metadata; TryFrom<FieldsWithMeta> adds lossily decoded metadata. (rust/lance-file/src/datatypes.rs:95-129; rust/lance-file/src/datatypes.rs:157-314)

```text
protobuf list, parents before children
|-- arena: childless Field + child node indices
|-- ID map: unique ID -> node; duplicate ID -> ambiguous
|   '-- ambiguous parent -> first pre-order DFS match
|-- reverse arena order: take children into parent
'-- roots in input order -> Schema(fields, empty metadata)
    '-- FieldsWithMeta adds the converted schema metadata
```

Unique IDs use expected-linear hash lookups; ambiguous references allocate a DFS stack and may lead to quadratic work. Parent-before-child is enforced, strict flat pre-order is not. Historical duplicates are intentionally retained: a nested duplicate under an earlier root can win over a root encountered earlier in the flat list. Missing parents produce Schema errors with name/IDs; internal arena failures are Internal. No Schema::validate or key/type check follows. Iterative reconstruction does not make recursive flattening or Field destruction stack-safe. (rust/lance-file/src/datatypes.rs:102-245; rust/lance-file/src/datatypes.rs:502-520)

Field metadata bytes are decoded with UTF-8 replacement; nonempty dedicated extension_name overrides its metadata key. Unknown numeric encodings become None; encoding numbers1..4 map Plain/VarBinary/Dictionary/RLE, and encoding writes None as0. The legacy field-kind number is ignored on read and forced0 on write. Primary presence uses positive position or legacy bool->Some(0); clustering uses positive position only and writes its legacy bool=false. Dictionary i64 locations cast unchecked to usize and back; loaded dictionary values are discarded. (rust/lance-file/src/datatypes.rs:11-94; rust/lance-file/src/datatypes.rs:316-344)

Minimal local conversion example, derived from the source doctest (not compiled here):

```rust
use lance_core::datatypes::Schema;
use lance_file::{datatypes::Fields, format::pb};
fn decode_root() -> lance_core::Result<Schema> {
    Schema::try_from(&Fields(vec![pb::Field {
        id: 0,
        parent_id: -1,
        name: "value".to_owned(),
        logical_type: "int32".to_owned(),
        ..Default::default()
    }]))
}
```

The example only establishes reconstruction; it does not validate a complete dataset schema. The source metadata roundtrip unit test uses Schema equality, which ignores top-level metadata, so that test alone cannot prove metadata preservation. (rust/lance-file/src/datatypes.rs:139-156; rust/lance-file/src/datatypes.rs:394-410; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:874-878)

## Encoding IO and retained memory

LanceEncodingsIo is public through the crate reexport. It owns a FileScheduler and starts with an8MiB read chunk target; the consuming setter accepts zero without validation. EncodingsIo promises one Bytes per input range including empties. This adapter preserves empty positions and original order, delegates priority unchanged to FileScheduler and always returns Some for optional bypass/stats handles. Stats replaces the extra recorder on a cloned scheduler; it does not reopen the file. (rust/lance-file/src/lib.rs:16-17; rust/lance-file/src/io.rs:12-50; rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:56-58; rust/lance-encoding/src/lib.rs:40-104; rust/lance-io/src/scheduler.rs:1336-1352)

For a range of length n>limit, generate k=ceil(n/limit) chunks: k-1 chunks of floor(n/k), then a final remainder. This is a target, not a strict cap: n=10,limit=3 yields2,2,2,4. Zero limit divides by zero for nonempty requests; reversed bounds subtract unchecked. No sort/dedup occurs. FileScheduler checks actual split start order, coalesces nearby requests and can split again, so this adapter does not determine physical IOP size. (rust/lance-file/src/io.rs:51-98; rust/lance-io/src/scheduler.rs:1195-1264)

Scheduler submission occurs before returning the adapter's boxed async block, including for an empty split list. Await errors propagate; result-count mismatch is Internal. Unsplit requests return the scheduler Vec directly. Reassembly groups returned Bytes per original request, inserts empty Bytes, cheaply clones single chunks and allocates/copies multiple chunks. It does not verify individual result lengths; retained source chunks overlap the combined allocation. Scheduler queue/cancellation lifetime remains pending. (rust/lance-file/src/io.rs:98-148)

## Exact-version dispatch matrix

Every dispatch takes ConcreteFileVersion; callers resolve Stable/Next separately. There is no ordered comparison or implicit nearest-version fallback. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/mod.rs:4-48)

| Operation family | V1 | V2_0 | V2_1, V2_2, V2_3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Field/name/whole-schema projections, physical counts and data-file column mapping | Own v1 module | Own module | Each own module |
| Current read projection / finish raw metadata | Internal | Own module | Each own module |
| Finish metadata index | VersionConflict(0,2) | Own module | Each own module |
| Decode embedded column metadata | NotSupported | Own module | Each own module |
| Validate global buffers | Successful no-op | Own module | Each own module |
| Copy external column | NotSupported, closure unused | Conditional callback | Always await callback |
| Finalize copied pages | NotSupported | Normalize pages | Successful no-op |
| Open projected reader | NotSupported | Full opener only | Eligible indexed attempt, then full on None |
| Create current/lazy writer; encode embedded/mini batch | NotSupported | Own module | Each own module |

Matrix evidence: rust/lance-file/src/versions/mod.rs:38-277; rust/lance-file/src/versions/mod.rs:285-401. Per-version byte grammars and concrete mechanisms are not inferred from this routing table.

External metadata validation checks whole-schema physical count, projection validity, sequential column.index values, then delegates rectangularity/normalized row count to the exact read projection. Indexed reader opening requires preference plus structural eligibility; an indexed error propagates, while None falls back. V2_0 never invokes the indexed closure. Self-described opening delegates optimistic-tail detection; OpenedFileReader::V1 only retains footer numbers, while Current owns FileReader. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/mod.rs:50-107; rust/lance-file/src/versions/mod.rs:279-326; rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:1117-1144; rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:1542-1555)

## Writer facade and diagnostics

FileWriter stores one boxed exact V2 writer. FileWriterOptions defaults all three Option fields to None; its local validator rejects only max_page_bytes=Some(0). The Arrow C-interface retention warning is documentation; current structural resolution uses 8 MiB per top-level field or a divided supplied budget, explicit max-page size before environment/default32 MiB, and keep_original_array=false. V2_0 uses the same local option resolution formulas (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:326-356). (rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:414-439) PAGE_BUFFER_ALIGNMENT=64 and LANCE_FILE_WRITER_MAX_PAGE_BYTES are declared here but used by concrete writers. (rust/lance-file/src/writer.rs:17-77)

write_batches awaits batches sequentially, stops at first error and does not roll back earlier effects. External-column initialization converts every ColumnInfo to protobuf first: both page encoding forms and column encoding become serialized prost Any in DirectEncoding; descriptor pairs unzip in order, page row counts/priorities persist, ColumnInfo.index is omitted. Only then is the concrete initializer called. The facade does not establish schema/column or state consistency. finish returns FileWriteSummary{num_rows,size_bytes}; abort returns unit; tell reports delegated position. Their durability/cleanup guarantees require concrete analysis. (rust/lance-file/src/writer.rs:79-115; rust/lance-file/src/writer.rs:160-289)

ExpectedTypes is effectively crate-internal despite pub declarations in its private module. It converts expected core fields to Arrow once, remembers the last successful SchemaRef, and compares schemas by value equality. It matches expected columns by name (same-position fast path, name-search fallback); absent fields and extras are outside this checker. It does not inspect array values/nulls. A failed check leaves the prior accepted schema cached. (rust/lance-file/src/writer.rs:17-21; rust/lance-file/src/writer/field_types.rs:67-114)

The recursive checker compares extension name/metadata when enabled, pairs Struct/List/LargeList/Map/FixedSizeList children by position, ignores names/nullability in those arms and ignores Map sortedness. Blob-v2 Struct/Struct short-circuits child validation after the extension gate; the blob encoder is responsible for descriptor checks. Utf8<-Utf8View and Binary<-BinaryView are directional exceptions. Other types use exact DataType equality, potentially including stricter embedded-field equality. Bare column writes skip only the top-level extension comparison; nested children still compare extensions. (rust/lance-file/src/writer/field_types.rs:115-193)

FieldTypeMismatch is publicly reexported and downcastable through Error::InvalidInput source. It retains expected/actual FieldRef and a path constructed from expected names. Dot separators are unescaped. Display prints type plus extension; metadata without an extension name prints as no extension even though comparison can reject it. Contextual concrete writers call type checks before encoder preparation/nullability checks; invalid bare column indices are guarded there rather than in ExpectedTypes::check_column. (rust/lance-file/src/writer/field_types.rs:21-65; rust/lance-file/src/writer/field_types.rs:120-193; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:610-630; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:663-689; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:458-477; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:544-572)

# lance-file runtime boundaries: schema, IO, exact dispatch and writer checks

**PARTIAL CRATE COVERAGE.** This supplement fully covers five local files (1,628 lines): datatypes.rs, io.rs, versions/mod.rs, writer.rs and writer/field_types.rs. Current composition/compression policies and shared structural reader are covered in the [composition supplement](rust-lance-file-composition.md). Exact current reader modules are covered in the [reader supplement](rust-lance-file-readers.md); V2_1/V2_2/V2_3 writers and shared pipeline are covered in the [structural writer supplement](rust-lance-file-structural-writer.md); the separate V2_0 writer and compatibility test/generator sources are covered in the [V2_0 supplement](rust-lance-file-v20-compatibility.md). The [shared reader](rust-lance-file-shared-reader.md) covers full/indexed metadata IO, caching and read dispatch; delegated scheduler behavior, binary fixture payloads remain pending. Source tests are described, not executed.

[File module](rust-lance-file.md) · [Orientation](../L0-orientation.md) · [Contracts](../L3-symbols/behavior-contracts.md) · [Format](../L3-symbols/format-spec.md) · [Scenarios](../L4-crosscutting/scenarios.md) · [Cookbook](../L4-crosscutting/cookbook.md)

## Schema reconstruction and persistence conversion

Fields(pub Vec<pb::Field>) and FieldsWithMeta{fields:Fields,metadata:HashMap<String,Vec<u8>>} are public. From<&Field> recursively flattens parent then children; From<&Schema> concatenates root subtrees. They preserve supplied IDs/parent IDs and do not validate or assign them. TryFrom<&Fields> for Schema reconstructs iteratively and supplies empty schema metadata; TryFrom<FieldsWithMeta> adds lossily decoded metadata. (rust/lance-file/src/datatypes.rs:95-129; rust/lance-file/src/datatypes.rs:157-314)

```text
protobuf list, parents before children
|-- arena: childless Field + child node indices
|-- ID map: unique ID -> node; duplicate ID -> ambiguous
|   '-- ambiguous parent -> first pre-order DFS match
|-- reverse arena order: take children into parent
'-- roots in input order -> Schema(fields, empty metadata)
    '-- FieldsWithMeta adds the converted schema metadata
```

Unique IDs use expected-linear hash lookups; ambiguous references allocate a DFS stack and may lead to quadratic work. Parent-before-child is enforced, strict flat pre-order is not. Historical duplicates are intentionally retained: a nested duplicate under an earlier root can win over a root encountered earlier in the flat list. Missing parents produce Schema errors with name/IDs; internal arena failures are Internal. No Schema::validate or key/type check follows. Iterative reconstruction does not make recursive flattening or Field destruction stack-safe. (rust/lance-file/src/datatypes.rs:102-245; rust/lance-file/src/datatypes.rs:502-520)

Field metadata bytes are decoded with UTF-8 replacement; nonempty dedicated extension_name overrides its metadata key. Unknown numeric encodings become None; encoding numbers1..4 map Plain/VarBinary/Dictionary/RLE, and encoding writes None as0. The legacy field-kind number is ignored on read and forced0 on write. Primary presence uses positive position or legacy bool->Some(0); clustering uses positive position only and writes its legacy bool=false. Dictionary i64 locations cast unchecked to usize and back; loaded dictionary values are discarded. (rust/lance-file/src/datatypes.rs:11-94; rust/lance-file/src/datatypes.rs:316-344)

Minimal local conversion example, derived from the source doctest (not compiled here):

```rust
use lance_core::datatypes::Schema;
use lance_file::{datatypes::Fields, format::pb};
fn decode_root() -> lance_core::Result<Schema> {
    Schema::try_from(&Fields(vec![pb::Field {
        id: 0,
        parent_id: -1,
        name: "value".to_owned(),
        logical_type: "int32".to_owned(),
        ..Default::default()
    }]))
}
```

The example only establishes reconstruction; it does not validate a complete dataset schema. The source metadata roundtrip unit test uses Schema equality, which ignores top-level metadata, so that test alone cannot prove metadata preservation. (rust/lance-file/src/datatypes.rs:139-156; rust/lance-file/src/datatypes.rs:394-410; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:874-878)

## Encoding IO and retained memory

LanceEncodingsIo is public through the crate reexport. It owns a FileScheduler and starts with an8MiB read chunk target; the consuming setter accepts zero without validation. EncodingsIo promises one Bytes per input range including empties. This adapter preserves empty positions and original order, delegates priority unchanged to FileScheduler and always returns Some for optional bypass/stats handles. Stats replaces the extra recorder on a cloned scheduler; it does not reopen the file. (rust/lance-file/src/lib.rs:16-17; rust/lance-file/src/io.rs:12-50; rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:56-58; rust/lance-encoding/src/lib.rs:40-104; rust/lance-io/src/scheduler.rs:1336-1352)

For a range of length n>limit, generate k=ceil(n/limit) chunks: k-1 chunks of floor(n/k), then a final remainder. This is a target, not a strict cap: n=10,limit=3 yields2,2,2,4. Zero limit divides by zero for nonempty requests; reversed bounds subtract unchecked. No sort/dedup occurs. FileScheduler checks actual split start order, coalesces nearby requests and can split again, so this adapter does not determine physical IOP size. (rust/lance-file/src/io.rs:51-98; rust/lance-io/src/scheduler.rs:1195-1264)

Scheduler submission occurs before returning the adapter's boxed async block, including for an empty split list. Await errors propagate; result-count mismatch is Internal. Unsplit requests return the scheduler Vec directly. Reassembly groups returned Bytes per original request, inserts empty Bytes, cheaply clones single chunks and allocates/copies multiple chunks. It does not verify individual result lengths; retained source chunks overlap the combined allocation. Scheduler queue/cancellation lifetime remains pending. (rust/lance-file/src/io.rs:98-148)

## Exact-version dispatch matrix

Every dispatch takes ConcreteFileVersion; callers resolve Stable/Next separately. There is no ordered comparison or implicit nearest-version fallback. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/mod.rs:4-48)

| Operation family | V1 | V2_0 | V2_1, V2_2, V2_3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Field/name/whole-schema projections, physical counts and data-file column mapping | Own v1 module | Own module | Each own module |
| Current read projection / finish raw metadata | Internal | Own module | Each own module |
| Finish metadata index | VersionConflict(0,2) | Own module | Each own module |
| Decode embedded column metadata | NotSupported | Own module | Each own module |
| Validate global buffers | Successful no-op | Own module | Each own module |
| Copy external column | NotSupported, closure unused | Conditional callback | Always await callback |
| Finalize copied pages | NotSupported | Normalize pages | Successful no-op |
| Open projected reader | NotSupported | Full opener only | Eligible indexed attempt, then full on None |
| Create current/lazy writer; encode embedded/mini batch | NotSupported | Own module | Each own module |

Matrix evidence: rust/lance-file/src/versions/mod.rs:38-277; rust/lance-file/src/versions/mod.rs:285-401. Per-version byte grammars and concrete mechanisms are not inferred from this routing table.

External metadata validation checks whole-schema physical count, projection validity, sequential column.index values, then delegates rectangularity/normalized row count to the exact read projection. Indexed reader opening requires preference plus structural eligibility; an indexed error propagates, while None falls back. V2_0 never invokes the indexed closure. Self-described opening delegates optimistic-tail detection; OpenedFileReader::V1 only retains footer numbers, while Current owns FileReader. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/mod.rs:50-107; rust/lance-file/src/versions/mod.rs:279-326; rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:1117-1144; rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:1542-1555)

## Writer facade and diagnostics

FileWriter stores one boxed exact V2 writer. FileWriterOptions defaults all three Option fields to None; its local validator rejects only max_page_bytes=Some(0). The Arrow C-interface retention warning is documentation; current structural resolution uses 8 MiB per top-level field or a divided supplied budget, explicit max-page size before environment/default32 MiB, and keep_original_array=false. V2_0 uses the same local option resolution formulas (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:326-356). (rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:414-439) PAGE_BUFFER_ALIGNMENT=64 and LANCE_FILE_WRITER_MAX_PAGE_BYTES are declared here but used by concrete writers. (rust/lance-file/src/writer.rs:17-77)

write_batches awaits batches sequentially, stops at first error and does not roll back earlier effects. External-column initialization converts every ColumnInfo to protobuf first: both page encoding forms and column encoding become serialized prost Any in DirectEncoding; descriptor pairs unzip in order, page row counts/priorities persist, ColumnInfo.index is omitted. Only then is the concrete initializer called. The facade does not establish schema/column or state consistency. finish returns FileWriteSummary{num_rows,size_bytes}; abort returns unit; tell reports delegated position. Their durability/cleanup guarantees require concrete analysis. (rust/lance-file/src/writer.rs:79-115; rust/lance-file/src/writer.rs:160-289)

ExpectedTypes is effectively crate-internal despite pub declarations in its private module. It converts expected core fields to Arrow once, remembers the last successful SchemaRef, and compares schemas by value equality. It matches expected columns by name (same-position fast path, name-search fallback); absent fields and extras are outside this checker. It does not inspect array values/nulls. A failed check leaves the prior accepted schema cached. (rust/lance-file/src/writer.rs:17-21; rust/lance-file/src/writer/field_types.rs:67-114)

The recursive checker compares extension name/metadata when enabled, pairs Struct/List/LargeList/Map/FixedSizeList children by position, ignores names/nullability in those arms and ignores Map sortedness. Blob-v2 Struct/Struct short-circuits child validation after the extension gate; the blob encoder is responsible for descriptor checks. Utf8<-Utf8View and Binary<-BinaryView are directional exceptions. Other types use exact DataType equality, potentially including stricter embedded-field equality. Bare column writes skip only the top-level extension comparison; nested children still compare extensions. (rust/lance-file/src/writer/field_types.rs:115-193)

FieldTypeMismatch is publicly reexported and downcastable through Error::InvalidInput source. It retains expected/actual FieldRef and a path constructed from expected names. Dot separators are unescaped. Display prints type plus extension; metadata without an extension name prints as no extension even though comparison can reject it. Contextual concrete writers call type checks before encoder preparation/nullability checks; invalid bare column indices are guarded there rather than in ExpectedTypes::check_column. (rust/lance-file/src/writer/field_types.rs:21-65; rust/lance-file/src/writer/field_types.rs:120-193; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:610-630; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:663-689; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:458-477; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:544-572)

# Exact current-version reader grammars

**PARTIAL CRATE COVERAGE.** This supplement fully covers four private exact reader modules (1,368 lines). It defines their local metadata acceptance, error ordering, normalization and projection behavior. Current structural writer lifecycles are covered in the [writer supplement](rust-lance-file-structural-writer.md). The [V2_0/compatibility supplement](rust-lance-file-v20-compatibility.md) covers the array writer and test/generator sources. The [shared reader](rust-lance-file-shared-reader.md) covers metadata IO, cache use and read dispatch. Delegated IO/decoder scheduling, byte decompression, V1 statistics algorithms, binary fixture payloads and Dataset integration remain pending. Source tests were read, not run.

[Crate](rust-lance-file.md) · [Composition](rust-lance-file-composition.md) · [Runtime interfaces](rust-lance-file-runtime.md) · [Orientation](../L0-orientation.md) · [Format](../L3-symbols/format-spec.md) · [Contracts](../L3-symbols/behavior-contracts.md) · [Tests](../L4-crosscutting/build-and-test.md)

## Accepted identity and validation order

| Reader | Full raw footer accepted | Metadata-index identity | Global buffers | Page representation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| V2_0 | (0,3) or (2,0) | V2_0 only | no-op | pb ArrayEncoding, normalized PageEncoding::Legacy |
| V2_1 | (2,1) only | V2_1 only | positions aligned64 | pb21 PageLayout, Structural |
| V2_2 | (2,2) only | V2_2 only | positions aligned64 | pb21 PageLayout, Structural |
| V2_3 | (2,3) only | V2_3 only | positions aligned64 | pb21 PageLayout, Structural |

Identity failures are VersionConflict before global-buffer/column work. Index mismatch diagnostics use the actual index enum's standard footer tuple, while full metadata reports original raw numbers. V2_0 preserves the accepted literal alias in cached major/minor alongside concrete V2_0 identity. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/reader.rs:350-395; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/reader.rs:215-258; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/reader.rs:217-260; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_3/reader.rs:255-298)

Full V2_1+ finish order is exact footer check, global alignment, column decoding, then cache-object construction. Metadata-index finish checks only identity/global alignment; it does not eagerly decode columns. All cached objects retain both original protobuf column metadata and normalized ColumnInfo plus raw schema, declared num_rows, descriptors, byte accounting and retained global bytes. No finish method reconciles these counts with schema/page rows/file size. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/reader.rs:350-395; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/reader.rs:215-258; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/reader.rs:217-260; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_3/reader.rs:255-298)

For V2_0, page Any must decode as pb ArrayEncoding, then page offset/size counts must match; column counts and Any are checked afterward. There is no page alignment or recursive ArrayEncoding grammar check in this module. V2_1+ decodes structural syntax, validates exact page grammar, then performs shared page alignment/descriptor construction; after all pages it builds ColumnInfo. ColumnEncoding envelope decoding is not a recursive column-grammar validator. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/reader.rs:30-133; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/reader.rs:161-176; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/reader.rs:163-178; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_3/reader.rs:201-216; rust/lance-file/src/reader/structural.rs:73-155)

Column batches decode serially, stopping at first error. A checked conversion guards each zero-based index, not the count itself: index u32::MAX is accepted, despite the diagnostic wording more than u32::MAX columns. Empty metadata slices are accepted locally. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/reader.rs:135-148; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/reader.rs:178-191; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/reader.rs:180-193; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_3/reader.rs:218-231)

## Compressive grammar: required children versus unchecked attributes

Across V2_1/2/3, Flat, InlineBitpacking and Constant compression variants succeed without inspecting widths, optional buffer-compression descriptors, literal bytes or other fields. Variable requires offsets; OutOfLineBitpacking, Fsst, ByteStreamSplit, General, FixedSizeList and PackedStruct require values. Dictionary validates indices first, then items. Each required child is recursively validated; missing compression oneof is InvalidInput. General does not require a compression descriptor here; cardinalities, dimensions, schemes, levels and numeric bounds are not generally checked by these visitors. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/reader.rs:18-100; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/reader.rs:18-106; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_3/reader.rs:18-89)

V2_1/V2_2 RLE require direct Flat values of8/16/32/64bits with data=None and direct Flat8 run lengths with data=None. They reject wrappers, 128-bit values and any present Flat.data buffer-compression descriptor, including a default descriptor. Flat.data is metadata, not a byte payload (protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:419-425). V2_3 instead recursively validates both child trees with the full grammar; it imposes no special Flat8 requirement. V2_1 rejects VariablePackedStruct outright. V2_2/V2_3 validate each packed field.value recursively and accept an empty field list at this gate. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/reader.rs:56-98; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/reader.rs:56-104; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_3/reader.rs:56-87)

These are local structural acceptance checks, not proof accepted data will decode. Recursive visitors and Blob-layout nesting have no explicit local depth limit; protobuf decoder restrictions are a separate, still unqualified boundary. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/reader.rs:26-159; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/reader.rs:26-161; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_3/reader.rs:26-199)

## Page-layout matrix

| Layout | V2_1 | V2_2 | V2_3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| MiniBlock | has_large_chunk must be false | must be true | must be true |
| FullZip | required value compression | same | same |
| Constant | inline_value absent; rep/def compression absent | validate optional rep/def; inline value unchecked | same as V2_2 |
| Blob | required recursively validated inner layout | same, exact2.2 grammar | same, exact2.3 grammar |
| Sparse | rejected | rejected | large-chunk and selective nested checks |
| Missing layout | InvalidInput | InvalidInput | InvalidInput |

MiniBlock checks large-chunk flag first, then optional repetition, optional definition, required value and optional dictionary encodings. This is an exact grammar boundary; selecting a newer reader does not mean it accepts the prior miniblock flag. V2_1 can read all-null ConstantLayout even though its composition page list has no constant() mechanism. Read acceptance and writer policy must be documented separately. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/reader.rs:102-159; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/reader.rs:108-161; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_3/reader.rs:148-199; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/mod.rs:125-134)

V2_3 Sparse requires has_large_chunk and value_compression. Positions are validated only when Explicit; missing sets, missing oneofs and other variants pass here. Validity delegates optional positions. List layers inspect nonempty positions, explicit counts and optional validity; FixedSizeList layers inspect optional validity only. A missing structural layer arm errors, but zero layers pass. Slot totals, ordering, ranges, dimensions and actual buffers are not checked by this visitor. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_3/reader.rs:91-146)

## Projection differences

V2_0 consumes a header column for every ordinary parent and then its children. Blob/packed fields are opaque. Schema-name selection computes the original whole-schema ID map before pruning, preserving original file indices. Missing mappings are silently omitted; complete schema is still retained. V2_1+ projection wrappers use the shared leaf algorithm with original schema mapping. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/reader.rs:177-232; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/reader.rs:193-213; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/reader.rs:195-215; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_3/reader.rs:233-253)

For V2_0, a comparable struct's child lengths must match its own header length; the error text about children also covers header/child mismatch. For nonstruct containers, child comparisons become disabled below that node, but the returned length remains the parent header length. The shared leaf algorithm instead derives a container's length from its first child. Both reject too few indices; production helpers reject surplus indices and require equal top-level normalized lengths. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/reader.rs:234-310; rust/lance-file/src/reader/structural.rs:278-357)

V2_0 prepare_projection accepts Full metadata after normal projection validity checks and clones metadata/projection, ignoring IO/cache. Indexed input gets structural validity errors first, then unconditional NotSupported. Its ReadProjection trait method awaits this no-IO preparation and then computes length. Accepting a V2_0 metadata index in finish_metadata_index does not imply indexed loading is usable. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/reader.rs:150-175; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/reader.rs:312-348; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/reader.rs:384-395)

## Local tests and change surface

V2_0 test_projection_length omits production's surplus-index check. V2_1 test helper delegates the shared version, which includes that check. Neither helper is a test case. The V2_1 single grammar test places empty VariablePackedStruct under General then FullZip and checks rejection text. V2_2 rejects a nested RLE using Flat16 run lengths; V2_3 accepts the same shape. It defines their local metadata acceptance, error ordering, normalization and projection behavior. Current structural writer lifecycles are covered in the [writer supplement](rust-lance-file-structural-writer.md). The [V2_0/compatibility supplement](rust-lance-file-v20-compatibility.md) covers the array writer and test/generator sources. The [shared reader](rust-lance-file-shared-reader.md) covers metadata IO, cache use and read dispatch. Delegated IO/decoder scheduling, byte decompression, binary fixture payloads and Dataset integration remain pending. Source tests were read, not run.

## Accepted identity and validation order

| Reader | Full raw footer accepted | Metadata-index identity | Global buffers | Page representation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| V2_0 | (0,3) or (2,0) | V2_0 only | no-op | pb ArrayEncoding, normalized PageEncoding::Legacy |
| V2_1 | (2,1) only | V2_1 only | positions aligned64 | pb21 PageLayout, Structural |
| V2_2 | (2,2) only | V2_2 only | positions aligned64 | pb21 PageLayout, Structural |
| V2_3 | (2,3) only | V2_3 only | positions aligned64 | pb21 PageLayout, Structural |

Identity failures are VersionConflict before global-buffer/column work. Index mismatch diagnostics use the actual index enum's standard footer tuple, while full metadata reports original raw numbers. V2_0 preserves the accepted literal alias in cached major/minor alongside concrete V2_0 identity. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/reader.rs:350-395; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/reader.rs:215-258; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/reader.rs:217-260; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_3/reader.rs:255-298)

Full V2_1+ finish order is exact footer check, global alignment, column decoding, then cache-object construction. Metadata-index finish checks only identity/global alignment; it does not eagerly decode columns. All cached objects retain both original protobuf column metadata and normalized ColumnInfo plus raw schema, declared num_rows, descriptors, byte accounting and retained global bytes. No finish method reconciles these counts with schema/page rows/file size. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/reader.rs:350-395; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/reader.rs:215-258; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/reader.rs:217-260; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_3/reader.rs:255-298)

For V2_0, page Any must decode as pb ArrayEncoding, then page offset/size counts must match; column counts and Any are checked afterward. There is no page alignment or recursive ArrayEncoding grammar check in this module. V2_1+ decodes structural syntax, validates exact page grammar, then performs shared page alignment/descriptor construction; after all pages it builds ColumnInfo. ColumnEncoding envelope decoding is not a recursive column-grammar validator. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/reader.rs:30-133; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/reader.rs:161-176; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/reader.rs:163-178; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_3/reader.rs:201-216; rust/lance-file/src/reader/structural.rs:73-155)

Column batches decode serially, stopping at first error. A checked conversion guards each zero-based index, not the count itself: index u32::MAX is accepted, despite the diagnostic wording more than u32::MAX columns. Empty metadata slices are accepted locally. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/reader.rs:135-148; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/reader.rs:178-191; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/reader.rs:180-193; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_3/reader.rs:218-231)

## Compressive grammar: required children versus unchecked attributes

Across V2_1/2/3, Flat, InlineBitpacking and Constant compression variants succeed without inspecting widths, optional buffer-compression descriptors, literal bytes or other fields. Variable requires offsets; OutOfLineBitpacking, Fsst, ByteStreamSplit, General, FixedSizeList and PackedStruct require values. Dictionary validates indices first, then items. Each required child is recursively validated; missing compression oneof is InvalidInput. General does not require a compression descriptor here; cardinalities, dimensions, schemes, levels and numeric bounds are not generally checked by these visitors. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/reader.rs:18-100; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/reader.rs:18-106; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_3/reader.rs:18-89)

V2_1/V2_2 RLE require direct Flat values of8/16/32/64bits with data=None and direct Flat8 run lengths with data=None. They reject wrappers, 128-bit values and any present Flat.data buffer-compression descriptor, including a default descriptor. Flat.data is metadata, not a byte payload (protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:419-425). V2_3 instead recursively validates both child trees with the full grammar; it imposes no special Flat8 requirement. V2_1 rejects VariablePackedStruct outright. V2_2/V2_3 validate each packed field.value recursively and accept an empty field list at this gate. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/reader.rs:56-98; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/reader.rs:56-104; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_3/reader.rs:56-87)

These are local structural acceptance checks, not proof accepted data will decode. Recursive visitors and Blob-layout nesting have no explicit local depth limit; protobuf decoder restrictions are a separate, still unqualified boundary. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/reader.rs:26-159; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/reader.rs:26-161; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_3/reader.rs:26-199)

## Page-layout matrix

| Layout | V2_1 | V2_2 | V2_3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| MiniBlock | has_large_chunk must be false | must be true | must be true |
| FullZip | required value compression | same | same |
| Constant | inline_value absent; rep/def compression absent | validate optional rep/def; inline value unchecked | same as V2_2 |
| Blob | required recursively validated inner layout | same, exact2.2 grammar | same, exact2.3 grammar |
| Sparse | rejected | rejected | large-chunk and selective nested checks |
| Missing layout | InvalidInput | InvalidInput | InvalidInput |

MiniBlock checks large-chunk flag first, then optional repetition, optional definition, required value and optional dictionary encodings. This is an exact grammar boundary; selecting a newer reader does not mean it accepts the prior miniblock flag. V2_1 can read all-null ConstantLayout even though its composition page list has no constant() mechanism. Read acceptance and writer policy must be documented separately. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/reader.rs:102-159; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/reader.rs:108-161; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_3/reader.rs:148-199; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/mod.rs:125-134)

V2_3 Sparse requires has_large_chunk and value_compression. Positions are validated only when Explicit; missing sets, missing oneofs and other variants pass here. Validity delegates optional positions. List layers inspect nonempty positions, explicit counts and optional validity; FixedSizeList layers inspect optional validity only. A missing structural layer arm errors, but zero layers pass. Slot totals, ordering, ranges, dimensions and actual buffers are not checked by this visitor. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_3/reader.rs:91-146)

## Projection differences

V2_0 consumes a header column for every ordinary parent and then its children. Blob/packed fields are opaque. Schema-name selection computes the original whole-schema ID map before pruning, preserving original file indices. Missing mappings are silently omitted; complete schema is still retained. V2_1+ projection wrappers use the shared leaf algorithm with original schema mapping. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/reader.rs:177-232; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/reader.rs:193-213; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/reader.rs:195-215; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_3/reader.rs:233-253)

For V2_0, a comparable struct's child lengths must match its own header length; the error text about children also covers header/child mismatch. For nonstruct containers, child comparisons become disabled below that node, but the returned length remains the parent header length. The shared leaf algorithm instead derives a container's length from its first child. Both reject too few indices; production helpers reject surplus indices and require equal top-level normalized lengths. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/reader.rs:234-310; rust/lance-file/src/reader/structural.rs:278-357)

V2_0 prepare_projection accepts Full metadata after normal projection validity checks and clones metadata/projection, ignoring IO/cache. Indexed input gets structural validity errors first, then unconditional NotSupported. Its ReadProjection trait method awaits this no-IO preparation and then computes length. Accepting a V2_0 metadata index in finish_metadata_index does not imply indexed loading is usable. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/reader.rs:150-175; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/reader.rs:312-348; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/reader.rs:384-395)

## Local tests and change surface

V2_0 test_projection_length omits production's surplus-index check. V2_1 test helper delegates the shared version, which includes that check. Neither helper is a test case. The V2_1 single grammar test places empty VariablePackedStruct under General then FullZip and checks rejection text. V2_2 rejects a nested RLE using Flat16 run lengths; V2_3 accepts the same shape. These last names mention variable width, but construct fixed-width Flat children, not a Variable node. Tests inspect grammar only, no file bytes or decompression; rejection tests do not assert error variant. No sparse validation fixture appears in the V2_3 file. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/reader.rs:397-415; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/reader.rs:260-304; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/reader.rs:262-308; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_3/reader.rs:300-341)

Changing nested grammar requires visiting every location that can contain a compressive child, including dictionary indices/items, optional level encodings, packed fields and explicit sparse sets. Keep read acceptance separate from the version writer cascade and maintain all stable contracts. These readers expose no plugin registration seam or environment configuration; ordinary module/trait composition is the extension boundary. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/reader.rs:26-159; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/reader.rs:26-161; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_3/reader.rs:26-199; AGENTS.md:7-17)
