# Current structural writers and shared pipeline

**PARTIAL CRATE COVERAGE.** This supplement covers all 1,697 lines of the V2_1, V2_2 and V2_3 concrete writers plus writer/structural.rs. It establishes their local initialization, mutation, IO sequencing, metadata spill and footer construction. The [V2_0 writer and compatibility source supplement](rust-lance-file-v20-compatibility.md) covers the separate array writer and fixture harness. The [shared reader](rust-lance-file-shared-reader.md) now covers local reader/cache orchestration; V1 statistics algorithms, delegated scheduling, encoder byte algorithms, backend durability and Dataset publication remain pending. Source tests were read, not run.

[Crate](rust-lance-file.md) · [Composition](rust-lance-file-composition.md) · [Reader grammar](rust-lance-file-readers.md) · [Runtime interfaces](rust-lance-file-runtime.md) · [Orientation](../L0-orientation.md) · [Format](../L3-symbols/format-spec.md) · [Contracts](../L3-symbols/behavior-contracts.md) · [Scenarios](../L4-crosscutting/scenarios.md)

## Ownership and initialization

Each public concrete Writer privately owns a StructuralFileSink, EncodingPipeline and CompressionParams. Its exact parent supplies encoding_strategy; the shared components do not select a version. Eager construction creates the same lazy object and initializes it before returning. Lazy construction only stores inputs. Initialization validates explicit options, computes runtime encoding options, validates schema, constructs BatchEncoder, then moves its encoders/mapping into the pipeline and initializes sink columns. The first write_batch infers a missing schema from Arrow, including for an empty batch. write_column only requires an already stored schema; it never infers one from a bare array. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/writer.rs:27-123; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/writer.rs:27-123; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_3/writer.rs:27-123; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:442-458; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:652-683)

```text
exact Writer
|-- CompressionParams -> exact field/page/compression strategy
|-- EncodingPipeline
|   |-- schema + ExpectedTypes + schema metadata
|   |-- field encoders + field-ID/physical-column mapping
|   '-- per-field row counts + maximum/aggregate row count
'-- StructuralFileSink
    |-- ObjectWriter + column metadata + user-global descriptors
    '-- optional page spill: Pending -> Active sidecar/chunk lists
```

These are ordinary owned fields with no local mutex, task spawn or Drop implementation. Both sink and pipeline expose crate-internal mechanisms that assume the wrapper maintains their relationship; they do not encode lifecycle state in the type system. (rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:50-58; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:132-177; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:381-455; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/writer.rs:32-36)

## Runtime options and validation

| Input | Actual local resolution |
|---|---|
| data_cache_bytes absent | 8 MiB per top-level field |
| data_cache_bytes present | integer division by top-level schema field count; remainder dropped |
| max_page_bytes present | supplied value; explicit Some(0) rejected before initialization |
| max_page_bytes absent | parse LANCE_FILE_WRITER_MAX_PAGE_BYTES as untrimmed u64; otherwise 32 MiB |
| invalid environment value | warning and 32 MiB; missing/non-Unicode value silently uses default |
| environment value 0 | accepted by this resolver; it is outside explicit-option validation |
| keep_original_array absent | false, distinct from EncodingOptions::default's true |
| buffer_alignment | 64 bytes |

The budget is divided by logical top-level fields even though one field may map to multiple physical columns. A supplied cache budget and zero top-level fields divide by zero before the wrapper reaches schema.validate. These are local formulas, not measured peak-memory bounds. (rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:410-439; rust/lance-file/src/writer.rs:56-65; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/writer.rs:78-84; rust/lance-encoding/src/encoder.rs:277-285; rust/lance-encoding/src/encoder.rs:332-365)

ExpectedTypes validates written fields by name, and encode_batch also selects by name; nullability instead zips batch columns against schema fields positionally. A reordered batch can therefore have nulls judged against another field's nullable flag. Recursive validation uses logical_nulls, intersects struct validity with inherited reachability, and ignores child nulls under a null struct parent. Nonstruct child-data recursion resets reachability and checks all exposed child slots; zip does not enforce equal child counts. (rust/lance-file/src/writer/field_types.rs:87-128; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:461-543; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:570-595)

## Batch and column mutation order

For write_batch: verify types/nullability; return for zero rows; reject a single batch longer than u32::MAX; collect all name-selected fields; call each encoder with its old field row number and a fresh RepDefBuilder; write out-of-line buffers; check aggregate u64 addition; advance every field counter and aggregate; await ordered page tasks and writer flush. The overflow check is after encoder mutation and possible buffer writes. A page or flush error leaves counters advanced. There is no rollback transaction around the batch. (rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:546-650)

write_column checks schema/index and the single array's u32 limit, then type/nullability and empty input. It encodes only that field, writes external buffers, performs unchecked per-field addition, and updates aggregate rows with max before awaiting pages. Unequal field lengths are supported locally; finish does not require equality. A contextual test writes lengths five and one, then expects a single-column projection to read one row and a joint projection to fail. That test covers V2_0/V2_1 and has not been executed here. (rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:652-703; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:725-801; rust/lance-file/src/writer_tests.rs:1084-1176)

FuturesOrdered preserves task output order; the sink writes one returned page at a time and stops at the first task/page error. Dropping remaining futures is visible here, but cancellation of any work they may have spawned is not established. The final flush comment describes observing already-failed uploads without waiting for all in-flight uploads; backend durability remains outside this analyzed scope. (rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:247-259)

## Alignment and metadata boundaries

Ordinary page, batch external, column and user-global buffers receive trailing padding of byte 0x48 to round their **length** to 64. This does not repair a misaligned starting position. write_external_buffer instead inserts leading zero padding based on current position and writes payload without trailing padding. Its returned start is aligned, but its end can leave the next ordinary buffer misaligned. Descriptors record payload lengths excluding padding. (rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:41-45; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:187-229; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:262-284; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:352-360)

Two finish-path assumptions are explicit in the source. First, finish_encoders writes out-of-line buffers raw, while the planner advances virtual positions by payload plus padding without modifying the payload. Second, column-buffer recording advances a local position by payload length while actual writes include trailing padding. Producers supplying multiple unaligned buffers would violate these recorded-position assumptions. This is a source-level deduction, not a reproduced failure or a claim that current producers emit that shape. (rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:725-765; rust/lance-encoding/src/encoder.rs:130-159)

Page metadata is constructed after its payload IO. Both Legacy and Structural descriptions are Any-wrapped into Direct encoding without exact grammar validation; length is encoded_page.num_rows and priority is row_number. The version reader later owns grammar acceptance. External metadata initialization replaces sink metadata and pipeline schema/declared rows without validating or resetting encoders, mapping, expected types or field counters. This path requires coherent caller-managed state. (rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:179-185; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:206-244; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:783-788; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/writer.rs:135-145)

## Page metadata spill

Configuring spill only stores Pending. The next write_page first writes payload bytes, then takes Pending and creates the sidecar. Creation failure/cancellation leaves no pending spill state in the sink. The sidecar encodes length-delimited Page messages into per-column buffers; each threshold is max(256 KiB / max(columns,1),64). A single page can overshoot, Vec clear retains capacity, and chunk descriptors keep growing. This is not a strict aggregate memory cap. (rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:47-112; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:170-172; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:231-243)

Finish takes all metadata/spill state, flushes and shuts down the sidecar, opens it, reads each column's chunks sequentially and reconstructs the entire page Vec for that column before serializing it. Existing metadata.pages are replaced, so enabling spill after pages have accumulated does not preserve them through this path. No local sidecar deletion occurs on success or failure. Errors after taking state do not restore it. (rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:312-340)

## Finish ordering and exact footer

All three wrappers perform the same sequence: flush buffered encoder pages; consume and finish field encoders; merge schema metadata and unload blob fields; write descriptor raw; serialize column metadata; write column offset table; write global offset table; append footer; shutdown object writer. The returned row count comes from pipeline accounting and size comes from shutdown. A never-initialized lazy writer reaches descriptor creation only after the empty flush path, then errors because schema is unknown. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/writer.rs:152-186; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/writer.rs:152-186; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_3/writer.rs:152-186; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:705-801)

Offset tables have no prefix: each entry is (position:u64 LE,length:u64 LE). The global table starts with descriptor entry0, then user globals in insertion order, even though their payloads were written earlier. Descriptor and column metadata are raw protobuf messages located by these tables; neither receives a length prefix or alignment padding here. (rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:279-309; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:343-350)

| Bytes relative to footer start | Value |
|---|---|
| 0–7 | column metadata region start, u64 LE |
| 8–15 | column offset table start, u64 LE |
| 16–23 | global offset table start, u64 LE |
| 24–27 | number of global buffers, u32 LE |
| 28–31 | number of physical columns, u32 LE |
| 32–33 | major version 2, u16 LE |
| 34–35 | exact minor 1, 2 or 3, u16 LE |
| 36–39 | ASCII LANC |

The footer is 40 bytes, with no checksum or count-range validation in these wrappers. The three minor literals are owned by their respective concrete writer. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/writer.rs:172-184; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/writer.rs:172-184; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_3/writer.rs:172-184; rust/lance-file/src/format.rs:33-33)

concat_lance_footer copies batch.data and appends an optional descriptor, per-column metadata and both offset tables before that same exact footer. It preserves supplied page/column offsets, ignores ColumnInfo.index and batch.top_level_columns, and does not check alignment, exact page grammar or buffer bounds. In mini mode the global table is empty. In self-described mode it clones the existing core Schema; unlike pipeline descriptor creation, it does not unload blobs or validate that schema. (rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:813-921; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:922-927; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/writer.rs:204-224; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/writer.rs:204-224; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_3/writer.rs:204-224)

## Errors, ownership and change consequences

finish is mutable rather than consuming, but is not made idempotent: field encoders and metadata are taken, schema metadata is drained, footer writes can partially succeed, and no finished flag guards another call. Each public abort(&mut self) is an empty async body. It does not drop the object writer; its comment about multipart cleanup on drop is not an implementation of abort. Backend cleanup behavior must be established separately before callers rely on it. (rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:312-340; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:725-801; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/writer.rs:152-191; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/writer.rs:152-191; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_3/writer.rs:152-191)

Private indexing/unwrap assumptions require schema, encoders, counts and physical columns to stay coherent. The final physical-column mismatch uses an unconditional panic; per-encoder counts use a debug assertion. No equal-field-length assertion is added. A new mechanism must preserve output count/order, address/padding correspondence and caller row accounting, and must not assume errors rewind state. (rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:546-568; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:610-649; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:697-701; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:725-776)

## Local tests and usage

Four helper-level tests cover hidden child null acceptance, visible child null rejection, dictionary logical-null rejection, and sliced-parent mask alignment. The two rejection cases inspect field-name text rather than Error variants. They do not test persistence, IO, spill, abort, overflow, footer bytes or reordered batch validation. Compatibility test/generator sources are now covered separately; writer_tests.rs is now fully analyzed in the [writer-test catalog](rust-lance-file-writer-tests.md), with its distinct integration oracles and limits. (rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:924-1025)

The following example uses the reviewed V2_2 API and was not compiled or executed:

```rust
use arrow_array::RecordBatch;
use lance_core::{Result, datatypes::Schema};
use lance_file::{versions::v2_2, writer::{FileWriteSummary, FileWriterOptions}};
use lance_io::traits::Writer as ObjectWriter;

async fn write_batches(
    output: Box<dyn ObjectWriter>,
    schema: Schema,
    batches: &[RecordBatch],

    let mut writer = v2_2::Writer::try_new(output, schema, FileWriterOptions::default())?;
    writer.write_batches(batches.iter()).await?;
    writer.finish().await
}
```

**PARTIAL CRATE COVERAGE.** This supplement covers all 1,697 lines of the V2_1, V2_2 and V2_3 concrete writers plus writer/structural.rs. It establishes their local initialization, mutation, IO sequencing, metadata spill and footer construction. The [V2_0 writer and compatibility source supplement](rust-lance-file-v20-compatibility.md) covers the separate array writer and fixture harness. The [shared reader](rust-lance-file-shared-reader.md) now covers local reader/cache orchestration; delegated scheduling, encoder byte algorithms, backend durability and Dataset publication remain pending. Source tests were read, not run.

[Crate](rust-lance-file.md) · [Composition](rust-lance-file-composition.md) · [Reader grammar](rust-lance-file-readers.md) · [Runtime interfaces](rust-lance-file-runtime.md) · [Orientation](../L0-orientation.md) · [Format](../L3-symbols/format-spec.md) · [Contracts](../L3-symbols/behavior-contracts.md) · [Scenarios](../L4-crosscutting/scenarios.md)

## Ownership and initialization

Each public concrete Writer privately owns a StructuralFileSink, EncodingPipeline and CompressionParams. Its exact parent supplies encoding_strategy; the shared components do not select a version. Eager construction creates the same lazy object and initializes it before returning. Lazy construction only stores inputs. Initialization validates explicit options, computes runtime encoding options, validates schema, constructs BatchEncoder, then moves its encoders/mapping into the pipeline and initializes sink columns. The first write_batch infers a missing schema from Arrow, including for an empty batch. write_column only requires an already stored schema; it never infers one from a bare array. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/writer.rs:27-123; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/writer.rs:27-123; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_3/writer.rs:27-123; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:442-458; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:652-683)

```text
exact Writer
|-- CompressionParams -> exact field/page/compression strategy
|-- EncodingPipeline
|   |-- schema + ExpectedTypes + schema metadata
|   |-- field encoders + field-ID/physical-column mapping
|   '-- per-field row counts + maximum/aggregate row count
'-- StructuralFileSink
    |-- ObjectWriter + column metadata + user-global descriptors
    '-- optional page spill: Pending -> Active sidecar/chunk lists
```

These are ordinary owned fields with no local mutex, task spawn or Drop implementation. Both sink and pipeline expose crate-internal mechanisms that assume the wrapper maintains their relationship; they do not encode lifecycle state in the type system. (rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:50-58; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:132-177; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:381-455; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/writer.rs:32-36)

## Runtime options and validation

| Input | Actual local resolution |
|---|---|
| data_cache_bytes absent | 8 MiB per top-level field |
| data_cache_bytes present | integer division by top-level schema field count; remainder dropped |
| max_page_bytes present | supplied value; explicit Some(0) rejected before initialization |
| max_page_bytes absent | parse LANCE_FILE_WRITER_MAX_PAGE_BYTES as untrimmed u64; otherwise 32 MiB |
| invalid environment value | warning and 32 MiB; missing/non-Unicode value silently uses default |
| environment value 0 | accepted by this resolver; it is outside explicit-option validation |
| keep_original_array absent | false, distinct from EncodingOptions::default's true |
| buffer_alignment | 64 bytes |

The budget is divided by logical top-level fields even though one field may map to multiple physical columns. A supplied cache budget and zero top-level fields divide by zero before the wrapper reaches schema.validate. These are local formulas, not measured peak-memory bounds. (rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:410-439; rust/lance-file/src/writer.rs:56-65; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/writer.rs:78-84; rust/lance-encoding/src/encoder.rs:277-285; rust/lance-encoding/src/encoder.rs:332-365)

ExpectedTypes validates written fields by name, and encode_batch also selects by name; nullability instead zips batch columns against schema fields positionally. A reordered batch can therefore have nulls judged against another field's nullable flag. Recursive validation uses logical_nulls, intersects struct validity with inherited reachability, and ignores child nulls under a null struct parent. Nonstruct child-data recursion resets reachability and checks all exposed child slots; zip does not enforce equal child counts. (rust/lance-file/src/writer/field_types.rs:87-128; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:461-543; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:570-595)

## Batch and column mutation order

For write_batch: verify types/nullability; return for zero rows; reject a single batch longer than u32::MAX; collect all name-selected fields; call each encoder with its old field row number and a fresh RepDefBuilder; write out-of-line buffers; check aggregate u64 addition; advance every field counter and aggregate; await ordered page tasks and writer flush. The overflow check is after encoder mutation and possible buffer writes. A page or flush error leaves counters advanced. There is no rollback transaction around the batch. (rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:546-650)

write_column checks schema/index and the single array's u32 limit, then type/nullability and empty input. It encodes only that field, writes external buffers, performs unchecked per-field addition, and updates aggregate rows with max before awaiting pages. Unequal field lengths are supported locally; finish does not require equality. A contextual test writes lengths five and one, then expects a single-column projection to read one row and a joint projection to fail. That test covers V2_0/V2_1 and has not been executed here. (rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:652-703; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:725-801; rust/lance-file/src/writer_tests.rs:1084-1176)

FuturesOrdered preserves task output order; the sink writes one returned page at a time and stops at the first task/page error. Dropping remaining futures is visible here, but cancellation of any work they may have spawned is not established. The final flush comment describes observing already-failed uploads without waiting for all in-flight uploads; backend durability remains outside this analyzed scope. (rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:247-259)

## Alignment and metadata boundaries

Ordinary page, batch external, column and user-global buffers receive trailing padding of byte 0x48 to round their **length** to 64. This does not repair a misaligned starting position. write_external_buffer instead inserts leading zero padding based on current position and writes payload without trailing padding. Its returned start is aligned, but its end can leave the next ordinary buffer misaligned. Descriptors record payload lengths excluding padding. (rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:41-45; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:187-229; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:262-284; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:352-360)

Two finish-path assumptions are explicit in the source. First, finish_encoders writes out-of-line buffers raw, while the planner advances virtual positions by payload plus padding without modifying the payload. Second, column-buffer recording advances a local position by payload length while actual writes include trailing padding. Producers supplying multiple unaligned buffers would violate these recorded-position assumptions. This is a source-level deduction, not a reproduced failure or a claim that current producers emit that shape. (rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:725-765; rust/lance-encoding/src/encoder.rs:130-159)

Page metadata is constructed after its payload IO. Both Legacy and Structural descriptions are Any-wrapped into Direct encoding without exact grammar validation; length is encoded_page.num_rows and priority is row_number. The version reader later owns grammar acceptance. External metadata initialization replaces sink metadata and pipeline schema/declared rows without validating or resetting encoders, mapping, expected types or field counters. This path requires coherent caller-managed state. (rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:179-185; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:206-244; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:783-788; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/writer.rs:135-145)

## Page metadata spill

Configuring spill only stores Pending. The next write_page first writes payload bytes, then takes Pending and creates the sidecar. Creation failure/cancellation leaves no pending spill state in the sink. The sidecar encodes length-delimited Page messages into per-column buffers; each threshold is max(256 KiB / max(columns,1),64). A single page can overshoot, Vec clear retains capacity, and chunk descriptors keep growing. This is not a strict aggregate memory cap. (rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:47-112; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:170-172; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:231-243)

Finish takes all metadata/spill state, flushes and shuts down the sidecar, opens it, reads each column's chunks sequentially and reconstructs the entire page Vec for that column before serializing it. Existing metadata.pages are replaced, so enabling spill after pages have accumulated does not preserve them through this path. No local sidecar deletion occurs on success or failure. Errors after taking state do not restore it. (rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:312-340)

## Finish ordering and exact footer

All three wrappers perform the same sequence: flush buffered encoder pages; consume and finish field encoders; merge schema metadata and unload blob fields; write descriptor raw; serialize column metadata; write column offset table; write global offset table; append footer; shutdown object writer. The returned row count comes from pipeline accounting and size comes from shutdown. A never-initialized lazy writer reaches descriptor creation only after the empty flush path, then errors because schema is unknown. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/writer.rs:152-186; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/writer.rs:152-186; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_3/writer.rs:152-186; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:705-801)

Offset tables have no prefix: each entry is (position:u64 LE,length:u64 LE). The global table starts with descriptor entry0, then user globals in insertion order, even though their payloads were written earlier. Descriptor and column metadata are raw protobuf messages located by these tables; neither receives a length prefix or alignment padding here. (rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:279-309; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:343-350)

| Bytes relative to footer start | Value |
|---|---|
| 0–7 | column metadata region start, u64 LE |
| 8–15 | column offset table start, u64 LE |
| 16–23 | global offset table start, u64 LE |
| 24–27 | number of global buffers, u32 LE |
| 28–31 | number of physical columns, u32 LE |
| 32–33 | major version 2, u16 LE |
| 34–35 | exact minor 1, 2 or 3, u16 LE |
| 36–39 | ASCII LANC |

The footer is 40 bytes, with no checksum or count-range validation in these wrappers. The three minor literals are owned by their respective concrete writer. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/writer.rs:172-184; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/writer.rs:172-184; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_3/writer.rs:172-184; rust/lance-file/src/format.rs:33-33)

concat_lance_footer copies batch.data and appends an optional descriptor, per-column metadata and both offset tables before that same exact footer. It preserves supplied page/column offsets, ignores ColumnInfo.index and batch.top_level_columns, and does not check alignment, exact page grammar or buffer bounds. In mini mode the global table is empty. In self-described mode it clones the existing core Schema; unlike pipeline descriptor creation, it does not unload blobs or validate that schema. (rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:813-921; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:922-927; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/writer.rs:204-224; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/writer.rs:204-224; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_3/writer.rs:204-224)

## Errors, ownership and change consequences

finish is mutable rather than consuming, but is not made idempotent: field encoders and metadata are taken, schema metadata is drained, footer writes can partially succeed, and no finished flag guards another call. Each public abort(&mut self) is an empty async body. It does not drop the object writer; its comment about multipart cleanup on drop is not an implementation of abort. Backend cleanup behavior must be established separately before callers rely on it. (rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:312-340; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:725-801; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/writer.rs:152-191; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/writer.rs:152-191; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_3/writer.rs:152-191)

Private indexing/unwrap assumptions require schema, encoders, counts and physical columns to stay coherent. The final physical-column mismatch uses an unconditional panic; per-encoder counts use a debug assertion. No equal-field-length assertion is added. A new mechanism must preserve output count/order, address/padding correspondence and caller row accounting, and must not assume errors rewind state. (rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:546-568; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:610-649; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:697-701; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:725-776)

## Local tests and usage

Four helper-level tests cover hidden child null acceptance, visible child null rejection, dictionary logical-null rejection, and sliced-parent mask alignment. The two rejection cases inspect field-name text rather than Error variants. They do not test persistence, IO, spill, abort, overflow, footer bytes or reordered batch validation. Compatibility test/generator sources are now covered separately; writer_tests.rs is now fully analyzed in the [writer-test catalog](rust-lance-file-writer-tests.md), with its distinct integration oracles and limits. (rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:924-1025)

The following example uses the reviewed V2_2 API and was not compiled or executed:

```rust
use arrow_array::RecordBatch;
use lance_core::{Result, datatypes::Schema};
use lance_file::{versions::v2_2, writer::{FileWriteSummary, FileWriterOptions}};
use lance_io::traits::Writer as ObjectWriter;

async fn write_batches(
    output: Box<dyn ObjectWriter>,
    schema: Schema,
    batches: &[RecordBatch],
) -> Result<FileWriteSummary> {
    let mut writer = v2_2::Writer::try_new(output, schema, FileWriterOptions::default())?;
    writer.write_batches(batches.iter()).await?;
    writer.finish().await
}
```

Construction, ordered borrowed batches and finish signatures are defined at rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/writer.rs:39-58, rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/writer.rs:101-115 and rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/writer.rs:152-186. The caller still owns Dataset publication and failure cleanup.

# Frozen V1 file reader

Complete local scope: all 1,562 lines of reader.rs, including 12 active tests and four helpers. Source tests were read, not run. The legacy statistics implementation, backend scheduling and complete Dataset lifecycle remain pending. Preserve this historical compatibility surface; new features belong in current-format paths. (AGENTS.md:13-18)

[Crate](rust-lance-file.md) · [V1 foundations](rust-lance-file-v1-foundation.md) · [Concrete codecs](rust-lance-file-v1-codecs.md) · [L2](../L2-files/rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs.md) · [Orientation](../L0-orientation.md) · [Symbols](../L3-symbols/symbol-index.md) · [Contracts](../L3-symbols/behavior-contracts.md) · [Scenarios](../L4-crosscutting/scenarios.md)

## Ownership and opening

FileReader shares its Reader, Metadata, ordinary PageTable and optional statistics PageTable through Arcs, while owning the supplied Schema. Clone retains shared underlying dictionary arrays through Schema's Clone behavior. object_reader is public and can be replaced without refreshing stored metadata. fragment_id is retained for Debug; this file does not generate row IDs. There is no custom Drop or shutdown protocol. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:41-66)

~~~text
try_new(store, path, supplied_schema)
`-- try_new_with_fragment_id(fragment=0, min=0, max=schema.max_id, cache=None)
    |-- ObjectStore.open
    |-- read_metadata
    `-- try_new_from_reader(metadata=Some)
        |-- ordinary PageTable load/cache using supplied path and bounds
        `-- statistics PageTable load/cache using Reader.path/stats
            `-- read_metadata again unless cache serves it
~~~

The two table futures are polled concurrently with try_join. Supplied metadata is trusted for ordinary-table loading; the statistics loader independently obtains metadata from the reader. Without a cache, ordinary construction reads metadata twice. The separate path, reader path, metadata, schema and field bounds are not reconciled. An error returns before construction; no rollback or explicit abort guard is installed. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:139-208; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:239-294)

Every constructor here requires Schema. It neither discovers schema nor hydrates dictionary values, despite stale documentation about an optional manifest. Self-describing opening is a separate table-layer trait: it reads Metadata, requires manifest_position, reads Manifest, populates schema dictionaries, then calls try_new_from_reader. Dataset fragment opening supplies its schema and file field bounds; the full Dataset wrapper remains pending. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:126-163; rust/lance-table/src/format/manifest.rs:1126-1182; rust/lance/src/dataset/fragment.rs:1374-1401)

## Cache and metadata contract

The private typed string key has stable schema `lance.file.previous.string-key`, version 1, and writes one string. Stable value IDs are `lance.file.previous.Metadata`, `lance.file.previous.PageTable` and `lance.file.previous.OptionalPageTable`; compiler type names are diagnostic only. The key contains no explicit schema, field bounds, fragment ID, object-store identity, ETag or file version. The supplied LanceCache may add a namespace; this local adapter adds no invalidation or persistent codec. Cached statistics absence is an Option value. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:68-123; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:181-198; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:239-288)

A cache miss reads the last min(file_size, block_size) bytes, extracts the eight-byte metadata position at footer[-16..-8], and either fetches the earlier framed struct or decodes its tail slice. That helper checks at least 16 tail bytes but does not check magic/version. Tail-position arithmetic and in-buffer framing do not locally guard malformed offsets/lengths; they can panic before decoding returns an error. Do not infer current-reader footer validation from this V1 path. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:210-234; rust/lance-io/src/utils.rs:221-231; rust/lance-io/src/utils.rs:248-263)

Statistics opening loads one batch covering field IDs 0 through max(leaf_field_ids), panicking on an empty leaf-ID list. page_stats_schema matches requested data IDs against parsed statistics root names, then projects their IDs and immediate children. It retains schema order and can return Some(empty). read_page_stats returns None for absent table or empty projection; otherwise reads batch 0. A disagreement between caller metadata and the independently loaded statistics table can reach an unwrap. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:239-267; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:398-445)

## Read APIs and scheduling

The method and free read_batch use the explicit per-call schema, rather than the stored reader schema promised by the method comment. Empty projection returns InvalidInput; the free-function comment about a with_row_id flag and panic is obsolete. No upfront subset/type validation occurs. Root fields are read with ordered buffered(reader.io_parallelism), and RecordBatch construction performs the final assembled-array check. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:324-335; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:485-507)

read_range immediately accepts any empty/reversed range as an empty batch, even beyond the end. Otherwise metadata splits across batches; reads are ordered and all results are retained. A single result is cloned; multiple results are concatenated in spawn_blocking. take first uses metadata grouping, which copies and sorts input, preserving duplicates but losing original order. It checks grouped batch IDs afterward, and its secondary offset check compares against whole-file length rather than batch length. Both APIs materialize the complete result; no local abort-on-drop mechanism is provided for blocking concat. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:342-396; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/format/metadata.rs:128-194)

batches_stream lazily filters ascending batch IDs and requests complete batches with fixed outer concurrency 2. It owns reader/projection through Arcs and advertises the supplied Arrow schema. Inner field reads retain their own Reader parallelism. This function does not spawn a Tokio task; a separately inspected Dataset ranges_to_tasks wrapper does spawn per-range tasks. Do not merge their cancellation or scheduling contracts. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:448-483; rust/lance/src/dataset/fragment.rs:158-186)

## Recursive reconstruction and edge cases

read_array dispatches by reconstructed DataType, not field.encoding: fixed stride first, then Null, the four byte-array types, Struct, Dictionary and the two variable-list widths. Unsupported types reach unimplemented. Every FSL enters fixed-stride dispatch regardless of its child; Interval has a width helper but is absent from that predicate. get_page_info reports missing field/batch entries as InvalidInput. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:509-576; rust/lance-arrow/src/lib.rs:111-181)

| Type/path | Local reconstruction | Relevant boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Fixed stride | Page position/length and selector go to plain codec | No field-nullability bitmap passed |
| Binary/string | Same, plus field.nullable | Equal offsets become null only when nullable |
| Dictionary | Plain keys plus cloned loaded values Arc | Missing dictionary/values unwraps |
| Struct | Sequential recursive child reads | No parent page/validity restored |
| Null | Synthesize count, no payload IO | End/max checks differ from plain; reversed range can underflow; Ranges panics |
| List/LargeList | Read offsets, read child values, normalize and build | Parent validity absent; reconstructed child is item/nullable=true |

Evidence: rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:559-808; rust/lance-arrow/src/lib.rs:202-229.

List range offsets include the terminal endpoint. Direct empty Indices accesses first/last and panics; public empty FileReader.take avoids per-column reads because grouping yields no groups. List Indices reads the whole first-to-last offset span, then sequentially reads each selected child range and concatenates; duplicates repeat those reads. Its offset lookup uses reader.page_table even when the function received another table, while child recursion uses that argument. Null selector validity is ignored on list and Null paths. Sortedness, arithmetic, child existence and offset coherence are caller/file assumptions. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:370-395; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:578-623; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:689-807)

The list constructor chooses a child field named item with nullable=true from actual child data type. It does not preserve arbitrary child metadata/name/nullability or parent nullness. Struct reconstruction similarly supplies no parent validity. These are frozen representation and reconstruction limits, not promises made by current-format readers. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:671-686; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:724-738; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:795-807; rust/lance-arrow/src/lib.rs:202-229)

## Tests, dependencies and extension boundary

Twelve active tests pin stable cache discriminator strings; seven-row multi-batch numeric/string/dictionary take; nullable empty-string conversion; combined-input struct/list roundtrip; one-row struct/list slice; Null lengths and weak is_err boundaries; List/LargeList take; sliced list equality plus file size<1000; one-batch numeric range; even-batch stream order; Boolean take with 256-byte blocks; and a narrow file opened under a wider schema with explicit field bounds. They do not prove malformed-file safety, cache invalidation, cancellation, parent-null preservation, arbitrary selectors or full multi-fragment behavior. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:827-1562)

The Boolean test is active reader-level coverage: 5,000 modulo-5 bits, indices [2,4,5,8,4555], expected [false,false,true,false,true]. It supplements the commented-out codec-local test and does not assert actual IO request counts. The projection test writes only f50 from a 100-field schema, then opens with full schema but min=max=f50; it does not test projection from a physically 100-column file. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:1459-1561)

Dependencies provide Arrow arrays/arithmetic/concat, borrowed async Reader/ObjectStore IO, Lance typed cache and metadata framing, tracing and boxed recursion/ordered futures. There is no local environment variable, Cargo feature, runtime registry, mutable global, unsafe block, durability commit or writer lifecycle. The generic offset type and private cache trait adapt existing implementations; they are not new-format plugin seams. Preserve historical behavior unless legacy repair is explicitly in scope. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:6-40; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:83-123; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:271-288; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:689-808; AGENTS.md:13-18)

# Frozen V1 file reader

Complete local scope: all 1,562 lines of reader.rs, including 12 active tests and four helpers. Source tests were read, not run. Backend scheduling and complete Dataset lifecycle remain pending. Preserve this historical compatibility surface; new features belong in current-format paths. (AGENTS.md:13-18)

[Crate](rust-lance-file.md) · [V1 foundations](rust-lance-file-v1-foundation.md) · [Concrete codecs](rust-lance-file-v1-codecs.md) · [L2](../L2-files/rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs.md) · [Orientation](../L0-orientation.md) · [Symbols](../L3-symbols/symbol-index.md) · [Contracts](../L3-symbols/behavior-contracts.md) · [Scenarios](../L4-crosscutting/scenarios.md)

## Ownership and opening

FileReader shares its Reader, Metadata, ordinary PageTable and optional statistics PageTable through Arcs, while owning the supplied Schema. Clone retains shared underlying dictionary arrays through Schema's Clone behavior. object_reader is public and can be replaced without refreshing stored metadata. fragment_id is retained for Debug; this file does not generate row IDs. There is no custom Drop or shutdown protocol. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:41-66)

~~~text
try_new(store, path, supplied_schema)
`-- try_new_with_fragment_id(fragment=0, min=0, max=schema.max_id, cache=None)
    |-- ObjectStore.open
    |-- read_metadata
    `-- try_new_from_reader(metadata=Some)
        |-- ordinary PageTable load/cache using supplied path and bounds
        `-- statistics PageTable load/cache using Reader.path/stats
            `-- read_metadata again unless cache serves it
~~~

The two table futures are polled concurrently with try_join. Supplied metadata is trusted for ordinary-table loading; the statistics loader independently obtains metadata from the reader. Without a cache, ordinary construction reads metadata twice. The separate path, reader path, metadata, schema and field bounds are not reconciled. An error returns before construction; no rollback or explicit abort guard is installed. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:139-208; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:239-294)

Every constructor here requires Schema. It neither discovers schema nor hydrates dictionary values, despite stale documentation about an optional manifest. Self-describing opening is a separate table-layer trait: it reads Metadata, requires manifest_position, reads Manifest, populates schema dictionaries, then calls try_new_from_reader. Dataset fragment opening supplies its schema and file field bounds; the full Dataset wrapper remains pending. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:126-163; rust/lance-table/src/format/manifest.rs:1126-1182; rust/lance/src/dataset/fragment.rs:1374-1401)

## Cache and metadata contract

The private typed string key has stable schema `lance.file.previous.string-key`, version 1, and writes one string. Stable value IDs are `lance.file.previous.Metadata`, `lance.file.previous.PageTable` and `lance.file.previous.OptionalPageTable`; compiler type names are diagnostic only. The key contains no explicit schema, field bounds, fragment ID, object-store identity, ETag or file version. The supplied LanceCache may add a namespace; this local adapter adds no invalidation or persistent codec. Cached statistics absence is an Option value. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:68-123; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:181-198; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:239-288)

A cache miss reads the last min(file_size, block_size) bytes, extracts the eight-byte metadata position at footer[-16..-8], and either fetches the earlier framed struct or decodes its tail slice. That helper checks at least 16 tail bytes but does not check magic/version. Tail-position arithmetic and in-buffer framing do not locally guard malformed offsets/lengths; they can panic before decoding returns an error. Do not infer current-reader footer validation from this V1 path. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:210-234; rust/lance-io/src/utils.rs:221-231; rust/lance-io/src/utils.rs:248-263)

Statistics opening loads one batch covering field IDs 0 through max(leaf_field_ids), panicking on an empty leaf-ID list. page_stats_schema matches requested data IDs against parsed statistics root names, then projects their IDs and immediate children. It retains schema order and can return Some(empty). read_page_stats returns None for absent table or empty projection; otherwise reads batch 0. A disagreement between caller metadata and the independently loaded statistics table can reach an unwrap. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:239-267; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:398-445)

## Read APIs and scheduling

The method and free read_batch use the explicit per-call schema, rather than the stored reader schema promised by the method comment. Empty projection returns InvalidInput; the free-function comment about a with_row_id flag and panic is obsolete. No upfront subset/type validation occurs. Root fields are read with ordered buffered(reader.io_parallelism), and RecordBatch construction performs the final assembled-array check. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:324-335; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:485-507)

read_range immediately accepts any empty/reversed range as an empty batch, even beyond the end. Otherwise metadata splits across batches; reads are ordered and all results are retained. A single result is cloned; multiple results are concatenated in spawn_blocking. take first uses metadata grouping, which copies and sorts input, preserving duplicates but losing original order. It checks grouped batch IDs afterward, and its secondary offset check compares against whole-file length rather than batch length. Both APIs materialize the complete result; no local abort-on-drop mechanism is provided for blocking concat. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:342-396; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/format/metadata.rs:128-194)

batches_stream lazily filters ascending batch IDs and requests complete batches with fixed outer concurrency 2. It owns reader/projection through Arcs and advertises the supplied Arrow schema. Inner field reads retain their own Reader parallelism. This function does not spawn a Tokio task; a separately inspected Dataset ranges_to_tasks wrapper does spawn per-range tasks. Do not merge their cancellation or scheduling contracts. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:448-483; rust/lance/src/dataset/fragment.rs:158-186)

## Recursive reconstruction and edge cases

read_array dispatches by reconstructed DataType, not field.encoding: fixed stride first, then Null, the four byte-array types, Struct, Dictionary and the two variable-list widths. Unsupported types reach unimplemented. Every FSL enters fixed-stride dispatch regardless of its child; Interval has a width helper but is absent from that predicate. get_page_info reports missing field/batch entries as InvalidInput. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:509-576; rust/lance-arrow/src/lib.rs:111-181)

| Type/path | Local reconstruction | Relevant boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Fixed stride | Page position/length and selector go to plain codec | No field-nullability bitmap passed |
| Binary/string | Same, plus field.nullable | Equal offsets become null only when nullable |
| Dictionary | Plain keys plus cloned loaded values Arc | Missing dictionary/values unwraps |
| Struct | Sequential recursive child reads | No parent page/validity restored |
| Null | Synthesize count, no payload IO | End/max checks differ from plain; reversed range can underflow; Ranges panics |
| List/LargeList | Read offsets, read child values, normalize and build | Parent validity absent; reconstructed child is item/nullable=true |

Evidence: rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:559-808; rust/lance-arrow/src/lib.rs:202-229.

List range offsets include the terminal endpoint. Direct empty Indices accesses first/last and panics; public empty FileReader.take avoids per-column reads because grouping yields no groups. List Indices reads the whole first-to-last offset span, then sequentially reads each selected child range and concatenates; duplicates repeat those reads. Its offset lookup uses reader.page_table even when the function received another table, while child recursion uses that argument. Null selector validity is ignored on list and Null paths. Sortedness, arithmetic, child existence and offset coherence are caller/file assumptions. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:370-395; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:578-623; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:689-807)

The list constructor chooses a child field named item with nullable=true from actual child data type. It does not preserve arbitrary child metadata/name/nullability or parent nullness. Struct reconstruction similarly supplies no parent validity. These are frozen representation and reconstruction limits, not promises made by current-format readers. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:671-686; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:724-738; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:795-807; rust/lance-arrow/src/lib.rs:202-229)

## Tests, dependencies and extension boundary

Twelve active tests pin stable cache discriminator strings; seven-row multi-batch numeric/string/dictionary take; nullable empty-string conversion; combined-input struct/list roundtrip; one-row struct/list slice; Null lengths and weak is_err boundaries; List/LargeList take; sliced list equality plus file size<1000; one-batch numeric range; even-batch stream order; Boolean take with 256-byte blocks; and a narrow file opened under a wider schema with explicit field bounds. They do not prove malformed-file safety, cache invalidation, cancellation, parent-null preservation, arbitrary selectors or full multi-fragment behavior. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:827-1562)

The Boolean test is active reader-level coverage: 5,000 modulo-5 bits, indices [2,4,5,8,4555], expected [false,false,true,false,true]. It supplements the commented-out codec-local test and does not assert actual IO request counts. The projection test writes only f50 from a 100-field schema, then opens with full schema but min=max=f50; it does not test projection from a physically 100-column file. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:1459-1561)

Dependencies provide Arrow arrays/arithmetic/concat, borrowed async Reader/ObjectStore IO, Lance typed cache and metadata framing, tracing and boxed recursion/ordered futures. There is no local environment variable, Cargo feature, runtime registry, mutable global, unsafe block, durability commit or writer lifecycle. The generic offset type and private cache trait adapt existing implementations; they are not new-format plugin seams. Preserve historical behavior unless legacy repair is explicitly in scope. # Frozen V1 concrete codecs

Complete local scope: binary.rs, dictionary.rs and plain.rs, all 1,815 physical lines. The 18 active test functions and five helpers were read, not run; three commented-out tests provide historical context only. The [full V1 reader](rust-lance-file-v1-reader.md) is covered; V1 statistics and backend lifecycle remain pending. Preserve these frozen compatibility surfaces rather than extending them for new format features. (AGENTS.md:13-18)

[Crate](rust-lance-file.md) · [V1 foundations](rust-lance-file-v1-foundation.md) · [Orientation](../L0-orientation.md) · [Symbols](../L3-symbols/symbol-index.md) · [Contracts](../L3-symbols/behavior-contracts.md) · [Format](../L3-symbols/format-spec.md) · [Scenarios](../L4-crosscutting/scenarios.md)

## Ownership and integration

Each encoder exclusively borrows Writer; each decoder borrows Reader. Plain and dictionary codecs also borrow DataType, while BinaryDecoder selects the Arrow byte-array type through its generic parameter and stores nullable. DictionaryDecoder owns an ArrayRef for already loaded values. Constructors store state without general file-bound or schema validation; DictionaryDecoder::new asserts the outer dictionary shape, and PlainDecoder::new unconditionally returns Ok. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:38-47; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:107-151; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:32-42; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:211-224; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/dictionary.rs:26-36; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/dictionary.rs:80-120)

~~~text
V1 writer page adapter
|-- PlainEncoder: primitive bytes / joined Boolean bits / recursive FSL values
|-- BinaryEncoder: payload bytes -> absolute Int64 position table
`-- DictionaryEncoder: PlainEncoder for keys only

V1 reader page adapter
|-- PlainDecoder: range IO -> array reconstruction
|-- BinaryDecoder: PlainDecoder positions -> payload range(s)
`-- DictionaryDecoder: PlainDecoder keys + supplied dictionary values
~~~

The page adapters store the encoder return as PageInfo.position and summed logical rows as length. Dictionary values travel separately through schema dictionary hydration; the reader adapter unwraps both dictionary metadata and loaded values before constructing its decoder. Complete local reader and writer lifecycles are now covered in their supplements; full Dataset/backend lifecycle remains pending. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:406-459; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:625-668; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:92-192)

## Binary layout and null semantics

For N rows, write the sliced payload spans in order, then N+1 absolute Int64 byte positions. Return the position-table start, not the first payload byte. The first position is Writer::tell before payloads; later array offsets are rebased to the current absolute end. The raw Int64 buffer is written without explicit endian conversion or framing. A nonempty list of empty arrays writes one endpoint; an empty input slice asserts. Exactly Utf8, Binary, LargeUtf8 and LargeBinary are supported; views return InvalidInput. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:48-105)

The encoder ignores original validity. Decoder nullable=true marks equal adjacent positions null, so valid empty values become null and null slots retaining nonempty payload cannot be distinguished from valid values. nullable=false returns all values valid, including empty spans. This is a frozen representation rule, not a universal null-preserving binary codec. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:61-86; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:165-232)

Range reads first fetch N+1 Int64 positions through PlainDecoder, subtract the first absolute position and cast offsets to Int32 for small byte arrays. Payload IO is skipped when start>=end; otherwise request that absolute byte range. Array construction is fallible, but negative/nonmonotone offsets and exact response size have no dedicated local checks. The internal endpoint assertion is weaker than the subsequent endpoint access. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:153-233; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:394-415)

## Selection rules and IO cost

| Behavior | BinaryDecoder | PlainDecoder and dictionary key reads |
|---|---|---|
| Empty range beyond logical length | Reject if end exceeds length before empty check | Return empty before bounds/type checks |
| Reversed range with end in bounds | Return empty | Return empty |
| RangeFrom starting beyond length | Return empty reversed range | Return empty reversed range |
| Multiple Ranges | InvalidInput | InvalidInput |
| Empty Indices | Typed empty, no IO | Typed empty, no IO |
| Take planning | Full first-to-last position span; fixed 64KiB byte-distance threshold | Reader block size; Boolean-specific block arithmetic |
| Ordering validation | Sorted-input assumption, no sorting; null index unwraps during sizing | Raw selector values drive planning without sorting or null preflight |

Selection evidence: rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:286-328; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:394-428; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:306-343; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:374-439; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/dictionary.rs:122-174.

Binary takes precompute the sum of selected value lengths, allocate payload and N+1 offsets, read planned chunks with ordered buffered(reader.io_parallelism), then copy a contiguous chunk once or gather each requested value. The position span can be large for two far-apart rows; a contiguous value run can exceed the nominal 64KiB threshold. Output is materialized even when the range-reader payload can share Bytes storage. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:246-390)

Plain takes keep consecutive rows in the same chunk regardless of block_size, and otherwise split by distance from the chunk's first row. Boolean takes split on row/(block_size*8). Both read enclosing ranges, apply Arrow take and retain all decoded chunk arrays before concat. The IO threshold is not a maximum request size; zero/truncated Boolean block sizes and unchecked arithmetic remain assumptions. FixedSizeList<Boolean> range decoding can recurse, while take calls byte_width, which is unavailable for its Boolean child. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:306-408; rust/lance-arrow/src/lib.rs:144-182)

## Repeated-leading-index discrepancy

The binary planner's condition is current==start_idx OR current-last_idx==1, where current is a relative row index and start_idx is a selector ordinal. For a nonempty value of length L and sorted indices [k,k], subtraction gives [0,0]; both iterations satisfy current==start_idx, leaving is_contiguous=true. The chunk reads/copies one value span L, but the output offsets and capacity count two values, reaching the debug assertion L==2L. Release execution reaches fallible array building with inconsistent offsets. This is an explicit source trace, not an executed reproduction. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:251-284; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:309-388)

The dense test includes a repeated later index and checks correct output; it does not include a repeated first index. Its standalone planner uses a 1024-byte threshold, whereas decoder.take uses 64KiB. Do not generalize that passing fixture into all-duplicate correctness or assume the tested standalone plan is the actual take plan. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:616-662)

## Plain bytes, recursive arrays and unsafe boundaries

Plain primitives write values only. Boolean inputs are joined bit by bit and None becomes false; other types use first-array byte_width and each array's offset/length to form an unsafe raw buffer slice. The configured DataType only selects FixedSizeList recursion; the primitive branch otherwise uses the actual first array type. It never validates that every later array has that type or enough bytes for the resulting span. Homogeneous valid Arrow arrays are a safety precondition: mixed narrower arrays can make the computed raw slice exceed its allocation. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:60-152)

Fixed lists recursively write sliced child values, discarding parent and eventual primitive validity. Read reconstructs them with parent validity None; fixed binary reads UInt8 values then builds a width-based array. Signed dimensions are cast and multiplied without local validation. Null primitive payloads are whatever the input values buffer contains, except Boolean's explicit false substitution; the compatibility fixture's zero/null-key expectations do not prove every possible null backing value is zero. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:73-152; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:252-304; rust/lance-file/src/compatibility_tests.rs:100-135)

bytes_to_array requires one value buffer. For FixedWidth, a short response is copied and zero-filled to (len+offset)*width; otherwise aligned Bytes can be retained and misaligned Bytes are copied. The resulting array has null_count0. This means truncated fixed-width input is not necessarily rejected: the active test supplies five bytes for three UInt16 values and expects the missing sixth byte to be zero. Bit-packed Boolean uses its separate buffer branch and starting bit offset. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:174-249; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:575-592; rust/lance-arrow/src/lib.rs:1536-1600)

These codecs perform unchecked pointer/offset/capacity arithmetic and have assertions/downcasts in public-call paths. No local transaction, rollback, flush/shutdown, abort guard or cancellation cleanup appears. Buffered futures preserve order and limit polling concurrency but do not prove backend cancellation; complete IO ownership remains pending. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:48-105; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:309-390; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:90-152; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:325-408; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/dictionary.rs:37-77)

## Dictionary keys and values

DictionaryEncoder supports all eight signed/unsigned integer key widths. It extracts each array's keys and writes them with PlainEncoder; no value comparison, dictionary merge/remap, value persistence or key-validity bitmap occurs. Supplying different dictionaries with the same key width therefore requires the caller to have already established compatible key meaning. DictionaryDecoder reads keys using PlainDecoder, clones the shared values Arc and calls DictionaryArray::try_new. Its declared dictionary value type is never compared with the supplied array; result value type follows that array. Keys lose stored validity through plain reconstruction, but dictionary values can independently be null. The one local test writes keys directly using PlainEncoder and never invokes DictionaryEncoder. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/dictionary.rs:104-174; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/dictionary.rs:187-252)

The foundation's binary-like predicate includes views, but both concrete binary encode and facade decode reject them. PlainEncoder can write fixed-width numeric buffers beyond integer widths, whereas schema dictionary hydration explicitly accepts only eight integer value types or the four binary families. These are different boundaries; do not infer symmetric hydration from write dispatch. Eight binary tests cover Utf8/LargeUtf8 multi-array/null roundtrips, one sliced offset, range variants, a simple take, million-row sparse/dense takes, repeated-write table positions and Binary null takes. Nine plain tests cover primitive raw-buffer roundtrips, Boolean joining, FSL/FSB and nested shapes, zero-padding, Int32 ranges/takes and usize chunk arithmetic. One dictionary test invokes eight key widths with supplied string values. Three disabled plain tests describe Boolean slices/nulls, FSL slices and Boolean takes; they are not executable coverage. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:431-710; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:442-852; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/dictionary.rs:177-253)

Untested local cases include leading duplicate binary indices, empty-vs-null binary values, mixed-array unsafe spans, null dictionary keys, inconsistent dictionaries/value types, invalid dimensions, all selector variants and error timing, and partial-write/cancellation behavior. Primitive test inputs reinterpret raw i64/f64 buffers for narrower types rather than numerically casting values; random float inputs are not pinned portable fixtures. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:485-710; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:456-490; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:717-851; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/dictionary.rs:187-252)

Dependencies are Arrow arrays/layout/casts/arithmetic/take/concat, Bytes and local BufferExt for ownership/alignment, Reader/Writer for IO policy, Tokio write extensions, ordered futures streams and async-recursion. Generic ByteArrayType and ArrowDictionaryKeyType select existing Arrow representations, not runtime codec registries. No local Cargo feature, environment variable or codec plugin hook is declared. Full Arrow and IO implementations remain outside this completed slice. # Frozen V1 concrete codecs

Complete local scope: binary.rs, dictionary.rs and plain.rs, all 1,815 physical lines. The 18 active test functions and five helpers were read, not run; three commented-out tests provide historical context only. The [full V1 reader](rust-lance-file-v1-reader.md) is covered; backend lifecycle remain pending. Preserve these frozen compatibility surfaces rather than extending them for new format features. ## Ownership and integration

Each encoder exclusively borrows Writer; each decoder borrows Reader. Plain and dictionary codecs also borrow DataType, while BinaryDecoder selects the Arrow byte-array type through its generic parameter and stores nullable. DictionaryDecoder owns an ArrayRef for already loaded values. Constructors store state without general file-bound or schema validation; DictionaryDecoder::new asserts the outer dictionary shape, and PlainDecoder::new unconditionally returns Ok. ## Binary layout and null semantics

For N rows, write the sliced payload spans in order, then N+1 absolute Int64 byte positions. Return the position-table start, not the first payload byte. The first position is Writer::tell before payloads; later array offsets are rebased to the current absolute end. The raw Int64 buffer is written without explicit endian conversion or framing. A nonempty list of empty arrays writes one endpoint; an empty input slice asserts. Exactly Utf8, Binary, LargeUtf8 and LargeBinary are supported; views return InvalidInput. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:48-105)

The encoder ignores original validity. Decoder nullable=true marks equal adjacent positions null, so valid empty values become null and null slots retaining nonempty payload cannot be distinguished from valid values. nullable=false returns all values valid, including empty spans. This is a frozen representation rule, not a universal null-preserving binary codec. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:61-86; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:165-232)

Range reads first fetch N+1 Int64 positions through PlainDecoder, subtract the first absolute position and cast offsets to Int32 for small byte arrays. Payload IO is skipped when start>=end; otherwise request that absolute byte range. Array construction is fallible, but negative/nonmonotone offsets and exact response size have no dedicated local checks. The internal endpoint assertion is weaker than the subsequent endpoint access. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:153-233; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:394-415)

## Selection rules and IO cost

| Behavior | BinaryDecoder | PlainDecoder and dictionary key reads |
|---|---|---|
| Empty range beyond logical length | Reject if end exceeds length before empty check | Return empty before bounds/type checks |
| Reversed range with end in bounds | Return empty | Return empty |
| RangeFrom starting beyond length | Return empty reversed range | Return empty reversed range |
| Multiple Ranges | InvalidInput | InvalidInput |
| Empty Indices | Typed empty, no IO | Typed empty, no IO |
| Take planning | Full first-to-last position span; fixed 64KiB byte-distance threshold | Reader block size; Boolean-specific block arithmetic |
| Ordering validation | Sorted-input assumption, no sorting; null index unwraps during sizing | Raw selector values drive planning without sorting or null preflight |

Selection evidence: rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:286-328; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:394-428; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:306-343; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:374-439; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/dictionary.rs:122-174.

Binary takes precompute the sum of selected value lengths, allocate payload and N+1 offsets, read planned chunks with ordered buffered(reader.io_parallelism), then copy a contiguous chunk once or gather each requested value. The position span can be large for two far-apart rows; a contiguous value run can exceed the nominal 64KiB threshold. Output is materialized even when the range-reader payload can share Bytes storage. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:246-390)

Plain takes keep consecutive rows in the same chunk regardless of block_size, and otherwise split by distance from the chunk's first row. Boolean takes split on row/(block_size*8). Both read enclosing ranges, apply Arrow take and retain all decoded chunk arrays before concat. The IO threshold is not a maximum request size; zero/truncated Boolean block sizes and unchecked arithmetic remain assumptions. FixedSizeList<Boolean> range decoding can recurse, while take calls byte_width, which is unavailable for its Boolean child. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:306-408; rust/lance-arrow/src/lib.rs:144-182)

## Repeated-leading-index discrepancy

The binary planner's condition is current==start_idx OR current-last_idx==1, where current is a relative row index and start_idx is a selector ordinal. For a nonempty value of length L and sorted indices [k,k], subtraction gives [0,0]; both iterations satisfy current==start_idx, leaving is_contiguous=true. The chunk reads/copies one value span L, but the output offsets and capacity count two values, reaching the debug assertion L==2L. Release execution reaches fallible array building with inconsistent offsets. This is an explicit source trace, not an executed reproduction. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:251-284; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:309-388)

The dense test includes a repeated later index and checks correct output; it does not include a repeated first index. Its standalone planner uses a 1024-byte threshold, whereas decoder.take uses 64KiB. Do not generalize that passing fixture into all-duplicate correctness or assume the tested standalone plan is the actual take plan. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:616-662)

## Plain bytes, recursive arrays and unsafe boundaries

Plain primitives write values only. Boolean inputs are joined bit by bit and None becomes false; other types use first-array byte_width and each array's offset/length to form an unsafe raw buffer slice. The configured DataType only selects FixedSizeList recursion; the primitive branch otherwise uses the actual first array type. It never validates that every later array has that type or enough bytes for the resulting span. Homogeneous valid Arrow arrays are a safety precondition: mixed narrower arrays can make the computed raw slice exceed its allocation. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:60-152)

Fixed lists recursively write sliced child values, discarding parent and eventual primitive validity. Read reconstructs them with parent validity None; fixed binary reads UInt8 values then builds a width-based array. Signed dimensions are cast and multiplied without local validation. Null primitive payloads are whatever the input values buffer contains, except Boolean's explicit false substitution; the compatibility fixture's zero/null-key expectations do not prove every possible null backing value is zero. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:73-152; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:252-304; rust/lance-file/src/compatibility_tests.rs:100-135)

bytes_to_array requires one value buffer. For FixedWidth, a short response is copied and zero-filled to (len+offset)*width; otherwise aligned Bytes can be retained and misaligned Bytes are copied. The resulting array has null_count0. This means truncated fixed-width input is not necessarily rejected: the active test supplies five bytes for three UInt16 values and expects the missing sixth byte to be zero. Bit-packed Boolean uses its separate buffer branch and starting bit offset. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:174-249; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:575-592; rust/lance-arrow/src/lib.rs:1536-1600)

These codecs perform unchecked pointer/offset/capacity arithmetic and have assertions/downcasts in public-call paths. No local transaction, rollback, flush/shutdown, abort guard or cancellation cleanup appears. Buffered futures preserve order and limit polling concurrency but do not prove backend cancellation; complete IO ownership remains pending. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:48-105; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:309-390; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:90-152; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:325-408; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/dictionary.rs:37-77)

## Dictionary keys and values

DictionaryEncoder supports all eight signed/unsigned integer key widths. It extracts each array's keys and writes them with PlainEncoder; no value comparison, dictionary merge/remap, value persistence or key-validity bitmap occurs. Supplying different dictionaries with the same key width therefore requires the caller to have already established compatible key meaning. The constructor's configured key type controls downcasts; unsupported types return Schema and supported types with an empty slice assert. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/dictionary.rs:26-77)

DictionaryDecoder reads keys using PlainDecoder, clones the shared values Arc and calls DictionaryArray::try_new. Its declared dictionary value type is never compared with the supplied array; result value type follows that array. Keys lose stored validity through plain reconstruction, but dictionary values can independently be null. The one local test writes keys directly using PlainEncoder and never invokes DictionaryEncoder. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/dictionary.rs:104-174; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/dictionary.rs:187-252)

The foundation's binary-like predicate includes views, but both concrete binary encode and facade decode reject them. PlainEncoder can write fixed-width numeric buffers beyond integer widths, whereas schema dictionary hydration explicitly accepts only eight integer value types or the four binary families. These are different boundaries; do not infer symmetric hydration from write dispatch.
