# Frozen V1 foundations: projection, dictionaries, metadata and page tables

Complete local scope: five files / 854 physical lines, including five tests. Concrete binary/plain/dictionary codecs are covered in the [codec supplement](rust-lance-file-v1-codecs.md); the [full V1 reader](rust-lance-file-v1-reader.md) is covered; V1 statistics and binary fixtures remain pending. These are historical compatibility surfaces; new capabilities belong in current formats/write paths. Tests were read, not run. (AGENTS.md:7-18)

[Crate](rust-lance-file.md) · [Current composition](rust-lance-file-composition.md) · [V2_0 and compatibility](rust-lance-file-v20-compatibility.md) · [Orientation](../L0-orientation.md) · [Symbols](../L3-symbols/symbol-index.md) · [Contracts](../L3-symbols/behavior-contracts.md) · [Format](../L3-symbols/format-spec.md) · [Scenarios](../L4-crosscutting/scenarios.md)

## Responsibilities and physical identity

The facade publicly owns encoding,format,page_table,reader,writer modules and V1 physical projection helpers. Its documentation declares accepted footer(0,0..=2) and write identity(0,2); the already analyzed exact-version parser maps those identities. The format child forwards metadata only. These files do not select current encoder strategies, commit manifests, publish a Dataset version or implement backend durability. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/mod.rs:1-24) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/format/mod.rs:1-4) (rust/lance-file/src/version.rs:172-272)

~~~text
v1
|-- mod: preorder Field IDs and physical-column projection
|-- encoding: value-codec dispatch and dictionary write/hydration
|   |-- plain / binary / dictionary: concrete codecs covered separately
|-- format/metadata: cumulative batch offsets and protobuf conversion
|-- page_table: sparse map <-> dense field-major pair matrix
+-- reader / writer: full local lifecycle covered in supplements
`-- writer/statistics: complete algorithms and tests pending
~~~

The tree follows the public module declarations and dependencies. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/mod.rs:10-23) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:16-33)

## Projection and field mapping

Visit fields in preorder, emitting the parent and then children. Blob and packed-struct fields each occupy one slot and stop recursion, while ordinary struct/container parents also occupy slots even when they have no data page. data_file_columns returns original signed IDs paired with consecutive signed physical indices from0. Counter/count arithmetic is unchecked. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/mod.rs:72-116)

The private BTreeMap casts IDs/indices to u32; repeated IDs retain the final column value. projection_from_field_ids clones the entire supplied schema into an Arc and appends only mapped fields, silently omitting missing mappings. It does not validate empty/repeated/out-of-bounds indices or remove unmatched schema fields. Column-name projection builds the full original mapping before delegating Schema::project, then selects original physical indices. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/mod.rs:25-71) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/mod.rs:93-116)

## Dictionary dispatch and mutation order

read_binary_array accepts exactly Utf8,Binary,LargeUtf8,LargeBinary, converts parameters first and dispatches to the corresponding BinaryDecoder; other types return InvalidInput. read_fixed_stride_array checks the local fixed-stride predicate, returns Schema on false, constructs PlainDecoder, then converts parameters and awaits get. Neither wrapper independently checks offsets or response sizes. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:35-90)

write_schema_dictionaries scans every ID from0 through max_field_id, skipping holes/nondictionaries. Missing dictionary metadata is IO; missing values is InvalidInput. The actual array type chooses numeric PlainEncoder or binary-like BinaryEncoder; unsupported values give Schema. Only successful encode updates offset/length. Earlier writes and mutations survive later errors; no transaction, shutdown or abort is provided. Cost includes sparse ID-span traversal and repeated schema lookup. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:92-132)

Hydration recursively processes nondictionary roots/children in order. For a dictionary it uses the schema value type, reads the entire stored region and replaces values, even when values was already Some. Binary values use nullable=true; only eight signed/unsigned integer types take the fixed-stride branch. It does not recurse below a dictionary node. async_recursion boxes recursion without explicit task spawning; successful earlier fields remain mutated on error/cancellation. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:134-192)

Write and read predicates are asymmetric. The write side asks is_numeric rather than the read side's explicit integer whitelist. The local is_binary_like also accepts Utf8View/BinaryView, which the four-type binary reader rejects. Concrete BinaryEncoder also rejects both view types; PlainEncoder writes fixed-width numeric buffers, while hydration retains its narrower integer whitelist. Complete codec contracts and test limits are now documented separately. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:91-105; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:90-115) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:47-70) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:116-127) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:143-176) (rust/lance-arrow/src/lib.rs:99-142)

The table manifest writer and schema-hydration adapter call these helpers only for ConcreteFileVersion::V1. The complete [V1 writer](rust-lance-file-v1-writer.md) now establishes provider/finish/error ordering: data page table, statistics, dictionaries/provider schema, Metadata and magics, followed by shutdown. (rust/lance-table/src/io/manifest.rs:212-230; rust/lance-table/src/format/manifest.rs:619-631; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:627-651)

## Metadata and logical row grouping

Metadata stores Vec<i32> cumulative batch offsets, usize page-table position, Option manifest position and optional statistics. Empty offsets report0batches/rows; otherwise batches=len-1 and rows=last cast to usize. push_batch_length seeds0 and appends an unchecked signed sum. Negative/zero lengths and malformed sentinel vectors are not rejected. get_offset can access the terminal sentinel; get_batch_length computes next-current with current default0, including the unusual negative-ID boundary. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/format/metadata.rs:14-33) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/format/metadata.rs:85-123)

Protobuf conversion clones offsets and statistics IDs, casts positions unchecked and flattens only statistics fields, dropping schema-level metadata. Missing manifest position encodes0, while decode always yields Some, including Some(0). Wire0 means externally stored manifest; the object converter does not normalize it back to None. Statistics schema decoding can fail; remaining shape/monotonicity/range validation is absent. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/format/metadata.rs:34-78) (protos/file.proto:25-93)

group_indices_to_batches clones and sorts input despite its sorted-input precondition comment. It preserves duplicate indices but loses original order, scans batch ends, groups in ascending batch ID and subtracts start offsets. Out-of-file rows can form terminal batch num_batches; nonempty indices with no offsets panic. range_to_batches unwraps the last offset and checks only end<=length, then binary-searches start cast to i32 and forms clamped subranges. Empty/reversed/overflow/malformed-offset cases are not fully guarded. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/format/metadata.rs:124-194)

These are helper contracts. The observed V1 reader returns an empty RecordBatch for Range::is_empty before calling range_to_batches, and take checks grouped batch_id against num_batches afterward. Do not turn a missing helper check into an assertion that every public reader call exposes it. The complete reader is now covered in the [reader supplement](rust-lance-file-v1-reader.md), including sorted grouping, selector differences, cache assumptions and constructor validation limits. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:342-396)

## Page-table representation and resource behavior

PageInfo holds position and logical length as usize; observed fixed/binary/dictionary writers use the number of array elements, not encoded byte count. PageTable privately owns BTreeMap<i32,BTreeMap<i32,PageInfo>>. set accepts arbitrary signed keys and overwrites; get distinguishes absent None from explicit Some(0,0). (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/page_table.rs:16-35) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/page_table.rs:147-160) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:393-459)

On disk, table dimensions are implicit: inclusive min..=max field IDs and num_batches from surrounding schema/metadata. Each field has consecutive batches, each containing position and length as signed64 values; missing/struct slots emit0,0. For valid dimensions, values count=2*(max-min+1)*num_batches and byte count=16*(max-min+1)*num_batches. No header or dimension vector is written here. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/page_table.rs:36-92) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/page_table.rs:94-145) (protos/file.proto:41-59)

load rejects max<min as Internal, then decodes the entire Int64 array and expands every cell into maps, including holes. Negative dimensions/values, arithmetic overflow and actual decoded shape are not independently validated; casts/downcasts/indexing rely on external invariants. Zero batches create nonempty outer maps with empty inner maps. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/page_table.rs:53-92)

write rejects empty outer maps and supplied min above observed minimum as InvalidInput. After tell it derives batch count=max batch key+1, builds two values per cell, writes the Arrow values buffer directly and returns starting position. The builder initially reserves only one element per cell. A loaded zero-batch table panics at the max-batch unwrap; sparse large IDs can amplify memory and bytes. This method has no explicit endian conversion, alignment, framing, flush, shutdown, abort or cancellation cleanup. It does not establish atomic persistence. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/page_table.rs:103-145)

## Tests, dependencies and extension boundary

Two metadata tests assert one index-group example and four valid range splits. Three page-table tests assert set/get, missing-cell zeros after write/read and three error variants/messages. The roundtrip test starts expected from actual.clone and overwrites fourteen holes; six populated values lack independent expectations. No local tests cover dictionary dispatch, projection edge cases, metadata object presence roundtrip, malformed offsets, negative dimensions, zero-batch rewrite or partial IO. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/format/metadata.rs:209-255) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/page_table.rs:162-287) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:186-192) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/mod.rs:102-116)

Dependencies are core Schema/Field/error/DeepSizeOf, file protobuf/schema adapters, Arrow arrays/builders/type predicates, IO Reader/Writer/ProtoStruct/ReadBatchParams, Tokio write extension and async-recursion. No local feature flag, environment variable or global mutable cache is declared. Reader/Writer/ProtoStruct are existing boundaries; these five files introduce no new extensible trait. Preserve historical behavior under the repository's frozen legacy policy, and use released historical fixtures for any explicitly required legacy repair. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:9-33) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/format/metadata.rs:4-12) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/page_table.rs:4-14) (AGENTS.md:13-18)

# Frozen V1 foundations: projection, dictionaries, metadata and page tables

Complete local scope: five files / 854 physical lines, including five tests. Concrete binary/plain/dictionary codecs are covered in the [codec supplement](rust-lance-file-v1-codecs.md); the [full V1 reader](rust-lance-file-v1-reader.md) is covered; binary fixtures remain pending. These are historical compatibility surfaces; new capabilities belong in current formats/write paths. Tests were read, not run. (AGENTS.md:7-18)

[Crate](rust-lance-file.md) · [Current composition](rust-lance-file-composition.md) · [V2_0 and compatibility](rust-lance-file-v20-compatibility.md) · [Orientation](../L0-orientation.md) · [Symbols](../L3-symbols/symbol-index.md) · [Contracts](../L3-symbols/behavior-contracts.md) · [Format](../L3-symbols/format-spec.md) · [Scenarios](../L4-crosscutting/scenarios.md)

## Responsibilities and physical identity

The facade publicly owns encoding,format,page_table,reader,writer modules and V1 physical projection helpers. Its documentation declares accepted footer(0,0..=2) and write identity(0,2); the already analyzed exact-version parser maps those identities. The format child forwards metadata only. These files do not select current encoder strategies, commit manifests, publish a Dataset version or implement backend durability. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/mod.rs:1-24) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/format/mod.rs:1-4) (rust/lance-file/src/version.rs:172-272)

~~~text
v1
|-- mod: preorder Field IDs and physical-column projection
|-- encoding: value-codec dispatch and dictionary write/hydration
|   |-- plain / binary / dictionary: concrete codecs covered separately
|-- format/metadata: cumulative batch offsets and protobuf conversion
|-- page_table: sparse map <-> dense field-major pair matrix
+-- reader / writer: full local lifecycle covered in supplements
`-- writer/statistics: complete algorithms and tests pending
~~~

The tree follows the public module declarations and dependencies. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/mod.rs:10-23) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:16-33)

## Projection and field mapping

Visit fields in preorder, emitting the parent and then children. Blob and packed-struct fields each occupy one slot and stop recursion, while ordinary struct/container parents also occupy slots even when they have no data page. data_file_columns returns original signed IDs paired with consecutive signed physical indices from0. Counter/count arithmetic is unchecked. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/mod.rs:72-116)

The private BTreeMap casts IDs/indices to u32; repeated IDs retain the final column value. projection_from_field_ids clones the entire supplied schema into an Arc and appends only mapped fields, silently omitting missing mappings. It does not validate empty/repeated/out-of-bounds indices or remove unmatched schema fields. Column-name projection builds the full original mapping before delegating Schema::project, then selects original physical indices. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/mod.rs:25-71) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/mod.rs:93-116)

## Dictionary dispatch and mutation order

read_binary_array accepts exactly Utf8,Binary,LargeUtf8,LargeBinary, converts parameters first and dispatches to the corresponding BinaryDecoder; other types return InvalidInput. read_fixed_stride_array checks the local fixed-stride predicate, returns Schema on false, constructs PlainDecoder, then converts parameters and awaits get. Neither wrapper independently checks offsets or response sizes. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:35-90)

write_schema_dictionaries scans every ID from0 through max_field_id, skipping holes/nondictionaries. Missing dictionary metadata is IO; missing values is InvalidInput. The actual array type chooses numeric PlainEncoder or binary-like BinaryEncoder; unsupported values give Schema. Only successful encode updates offset/length. Earlier writes and mutations survive later errors; no transaction, shutdown or abort is provided. Cost includes sparse ID-span traversal and repeated schema lookup. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:92-132)

Hydration recursively processes nondictionary roots/children in order. For a dictionary it uses the schema value type, reads the entire stored region and replaces values, even when values was already Some. Binary values use nullable=true; only eight signed/unsigned integer types take the fixed-stride branch. It does not recurse below a dictionary node. async_recursion boxes recursion without explicit task spawning; successful earlier fields remain mutated on error/cancellation. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:134-192)

Write and read predicates are asymmetric. The write side asks is_numeric rather than the read side's explicit integer whitelist. The local is_binary_like also accepts Utf8View/BinaryView, which the four-type binary reader rejects. Concrete BinaryEncoder also rejects both view types; PlainEncoder writes fixed-width numeric buffers, while hydration retains its narrower integer whitelist. Complete codec contracts and test limits are now documented separately. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:91-105; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:90-115) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:47-70) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:116-127) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:143-176) (rust/lance-arrow/src/lib.rs:99-142)

The table manifest writer and schema-hydration adapter call these helpers only for ConcreteFileVersion::V1. The complete [V1 writer](rust-lance-file-v1-writer.md) now establishes provider/finish/error ordering: data page table, statistics, dictionaries/provider schema, Metadata and magics, followed by shutdown. (rust/lance-table/src/io/manifest.rs:212-230; rust/lance-table/src/format/manifest.rs:619-631; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:627-651)

## Metadata and logical row grouping

Metadata stores Vec<i32> cumulative batch offsets, usize page-table position, Option manifest position and optional statistics. Empty offsets report0batches/rows; otherwise batches=len-1 and rows=last cast to usize. push_batch_length seeds0 and appends an unchecked signed sum. Negative/zero lengths and malformed sentinel vectors are not rejected. get_offset can access the terminal sentinel; get_batch_length computes next-current with current default0, including the unusual negative-ID boundary. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/format/metadata.rs:14-33) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/format/metadata.rs:85-123)

Protobuf conversion clones offsets and statistics IDs, casts positions unchecked and flattens only statistics fields, dropping schema-level metadata. Missing manifest position encodes0, while decode always yields Some, including Some(0). Wire0 means externally stored manifest; the object converter does not normalize it back to None. Statistics schema decoding can fail; remaining shape/monotonicity/range validation is absent. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/format/metadata.rs:34-78) (protos/file.proto:25-93)

group_indices_to_batches clones and sorts input despite its sorted-input precondition comment. It preserves duplicate indices but loses original order, scans batch ends, groups in ascending batch ID and subtracts start offsets. Out-of-file rows can form terminal batch num_batches; nonempty indices with no offsets panic. range_to_batches unwraps the last offset and checks only end<=length, then binary-searches start cast to i32 and forms clamped subranges. Empty/reversed/overflow/malformed-offset cases are not fully guarded. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/format/metadata.rs:124-194)

These are helper contracts. The observed V1 reader returns an empty RecordBatch for Range::is_empty before calling range_to_batches, and take checks grouped batch_id against num_batches afterward. Do not turn a missing helper check into an assertion that every public reader call exposes it. The complete reader is now covered in the [reader supplement](rust-lance-file-v1-reader.md), including sorted grouping, selector differences, cache assumptions and constructor validation limits. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:342-396)

## Page-table representation and resource behavior

PageInfo holds position and logical length as usize; observed fixed/binary/dictionary writers use the number of array elements, not encoded byte count. PageTable privately owns BTreeMap<i32,BTreeMap<i32,PageInfo>>. set accepts arbitrary signed keys and overwrites; get distinguishes absent None from explicit Some(0,0). (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/page_table.rs:16-35) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/page_table.rs:147-160) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:393-459)

On disk, table dimensions are implicit: inclusive min..=max field IDs and num_batches from surrounding schema/metadata. Each field has consecutive batches, each containing position and length as signed64 values; missing/struct slots emit0,0. For valid dimensions, values count=2*(max-min+1)*num_batches and byte count=16*(max-min+1)*num_batches. No header or dimension vector is written here. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/page_table.rs:36-92) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/page_table.rs:94-145) (protos/file.proto:41-59)

load rejects max<min as Internal, then decodes the entire Int64 array and expands every cell into maps, including holes. Negative dimensions/values, arithmetic overflow and actual decoded shape are not independently validated; casts/downcasts/indexing rely on external invariants. Zero batches create nonempty outer maps with empty inner maps. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/page_table.rs:53-92)

write rejects empty outer maps and supplied min above observed minimum as InvalidInput. After tell it derives batch count=max batch key+1, builds two values per cell, writes the Arrow values buffer directly and returns starting position. The builder initially reserves only one element per cell. A loaded zero-batch table panics at the max-batch unwrap; sparse large IDs can amplify memory and bytes. This method has no explicit endian conversion, alignment, framing, flush, shutdown, abort or cancellation cleanup. It does not establish atomic persistence. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/page_table.rs:103-145)

## Tests, dependencies and extension boundary

Two metadata tests assert one index-group example and four valid range splits. Three page-table tests assert set/get, missing-cell zeros after write/read and three error variants/messages. The roundtrip test starts expected from actual.clone and overwrites fourteen holes; six populated values lack independent expectations. No local tests cover dictionary dispatch, projection edge cases, metadata object presence roundtrip, malformed offsets, negative dimensions, zero-batch rewrite or partial IO. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/format/metadata.rs:209-255) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/page_table.rs:162-287) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:186-192) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/mod.rs:102-116)

Dependencies are core Schema/Field/error/DeepSizeOf, file protobuf/schema adapters, Arrow arrays/builders/type predicates, IO Reader/Writer/ProtoStruct/ReadBatchParams, Tokio write extension and async-recursion. No local feature flag, environment variable or global mutable cache is declared. Reader/Writer/ProtoStruct are existing boundaries; these five files introduce no new extensible trait. Preserve historical behavior under the repository's frozen legacy policy, and use released historical fixtures for any explicitly required legacy repair. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:9-33) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/format/metadata.rs:4-12) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/page_table.rs:4-14) (AGENTS.md:13-18)

# lance-file: file versions and entry points

**INCOMPLETE.** Forty-eight of 56 inventory entries are analyzed (25,031 physical text/symlink lines). Schema conversion, encoding IO adapter, exact dispatch, current-version composition/compression selection, shared structural projection, writer facade and type checks are covered. Exact current reader metadata/projection modules and V2_1/V2_2/V2_3 writer wrappers/shared pipeline are covered; V2_0 writer, testing utilities and compatibility test/generator sources are covered in the [V2_0/compatibility supplement](rust-lance-file-v20-compatibility.md). The complete [writer-test catalog](rust-lance-file-writer-tests.md) is also covered. The [shared reader](rust-lance-file-shared-reader.md) now covers full/indexed metadata loading, local caching, read dispatch and tests. The [concat supplement](rust-lance-file-concat.md) covers complete-file assembly and Blob part validation. The [V1 foundation supplement](rust-lance-file-v1-foundation.md) covers projection, dictionary dispatch, metadata and page tables; the [V1 concrete codec supplement](rust-lance-file-v1-codecs.md) covers binary/plain/dictionary implementations. The [full V1 reader](rust-lance-file-v1-reader.md) and [V1 writer](rust-lance-file-v1-writer.md), including its [full statistics implementation](rust-lance-file-v1-statistics.md), are covered; modern encoding/IO scheduler implementations, binary fixture payloads and benches remain pending. README describes an internal crate not intended for external use, despite public Rust modules. (rust/lance-file/README.md:1-6)

[Orientation](../L0-orientation.md) · [Table metadata](rust-lance-table.md) · [Format](../L3-symbols/format-spec.md) · [Scenarios](../L4-crosscutting/scenarios.md) · [Build/test](../L4-crosscutting/build-and-test.md)

## Responsibility and routes

The crate declares readers/writers for the Lance file format. Its facade exports concat,datatypes,format,reader,testing,version,versions,writer; io is crate-visible with LanceEncodingsIo publicly reexported; compatibility_tests is private under cfg(test). The [runtime-boundary supplement](rust-lance-file-runtime.md) covers schema conversion, IO adaptation, exact dispatch and writer interfaces; the [structural writer supplement](rust-lance-file-structural-writer.md) covers current structural writer lifecycles, and the [V2_0/compatibility supplement](rust-lance-file-v20-compatibility.md) covers the separate array writer and fixture harness. Shared reader loading/cache/projection orchestration is covered in the [shared reader supplement](rust-lance-file-shared-reader.md); V1 foundations and concrete binary/plain/dictionary codecs are covered separately; the [full V1 reader](rust-lance-file-v1-reader.md) is covered. Delegated modern encoding/IO scheduling remain pending. (rust/lance-file/README.md:3-6; rust/lance-file/src/lib.rs:4-17)

```text
lance_file
|-- version: request policy -> exact identity -> metadata/footer codecs
|-- determine_file_version: size -> last8 bytes -> magic -> exact identity
|-- format: generated pb / pbfile, LANC magic and legacy0.2 constants
|-- io: range splitting, empty placeholders and ordered reassembly
|-- datatypes: flat protobuf fields <-> core schema trees
|-- versions: exact dispatch, composition/policies, current reader grammar and all exact V2 writers
|   `-- v1: projection/dictionary dispatch/metadata/page table covered; concrete implementations pending
|-- writer: facade/options/type checks and shared structural pipeline covered
|-- reader: full/indexed metadata, cache, projections, read dispatch and tests covered
|-- concat: compatibility, Blob part gates, page relocation and output lifecycle
|-- testing: public local-file/cache helpers, collecting IO
`-- compatibility_tests: private cfg(test), pinned stable bytes / current unstable determinism
```

Routes follow rust/lance-file/src/lib.rs:4-60 and rust/lance-file/src/version.rs:19-262. No capability is inferred from numeric release order.

See [current composition and structural projection](rust-lance-file-composition.md) for ordered version policies and shared metadata contracts.

See [exact reader grammar](rust-lance-file-readers.md) for metadata validation order and version-specific acceptance.

## Caller requests and persisted identities

LanceFileVersion is a caller selector with Legacy,V2_0,V2_1,Stable,V2_2,Next,V2_3. Default is exact V2_2. resolve() maps Stable->V2_2,Next->V2_3 and exact variants to themselves (Legacy->V1). is_unstable is true only after resolving to V2_3. Display/serde preserve stable/next as strings; they are request serialization, not strict persisted identity codecs. (rust/lance-file/src/version.rs:19-127)

FromStr lowercases but does not trim. Accepted aliases are0.1/legacy,2.0/0.3,2.1,2.2,2.3,stable,next. ConcreteFileVersion has only V1,V2_0,V2_1,V2_2,V2_3, derives Hash but no ordering, and has no Default/serde/FromStr implementation here. Strict from_manifest_string accepts canonical0.1/2.0/2.1/2.2/2.3 only. to_selector always produces exact variants, losing prior policy intent. | V1 |0.1 |(0,2) |(0,2) |(0,2) |
| V2_0 |2.0 |(2,0) |(0,3) |(2,0) |
| V2_1 |2.1 |(2,1) |(2,1) |(2,1) |
| V2_2 |2.2 |(2,2) |(2,2) |(2,2) |

Both numeric decoders accept(0,0..=2) as V1 and(0,3)/(2,0) as V2_0, plus the other listed exact pairs. They reject everything else with InvalidInput Unknown Lance storage version: value. Strict string decoding rejects0.3 even though request parsing and numeric footer alias handling accept their respective historical forms. The table describes mapping functions, not proof every writer calls them. (rust/lance-file/src/version.rs:172-272)

## Footer detection and errors

determine_file_version takes ObjectStore,Path,optional known usize size. If unknown, await store.size and checked-convert; if known, trust it. Reject size<8, await open_with_size and get_range(size-8..size), require footer[4..]==LANC, decode first four bytes as LEu16 major/minor and dispatch exact parser. IO errors propagate; size/magic/version errors are InvalidInput. Fewer than4 returned bytes could panic because no explicit received-length check precedes slicing. (rust/lance-file/src/lib.rs:25-60; rust/lance-file/src/format.rs:30-33)

This reads only the final8 bytes and does not verify pages, schema, full footer structure or data validity. The local async fixture uses synthetic8-byte legacy footers with no data. Known size avoids the explicit size call, but underlying store.open behavior and total request count remain pending. (rust/lance-file/src/lib.rs:30-59; rust/lance-file/src/version.rs:411-430)

Runtime dependencies declare Lance Arrow/core/encoding/IO, Arrow arithmetic/array/buffer/cast/data/schema/select, async-recursion/async-trait, byteorder/bytes, datafusion-common, futures/log/num-traits, object_store,prost/prost-types,serde,tokio,tracing. Dev dependencies are lance-datagen,lance-testing,criterion,rstest,proptest,pretty_assertions,rand,test-log,libc. The protos symlink targets ../../protos/. format::pb and pbfile include generated lance.file.rs and lance.file.v2.rs. No build/install was performed. ## Extension boundary

Keep caller selectors distinct from exact storage identities; a new exact version needs explicit string/data-metadata/standard-footer/embedded-footer mapping and explicit capabilities elsewhere. Do not infer support by ordering, persist Stable/Next in manifests, or collapse the v2.0 footer alias distinction. The local tests pin these mappings but do not establish full historical reader/writer compatibility. Exact reader/writer dispatch and shared type checks are now covered in the runtime-boundary supplement; all exact V2 writer mechanisms and compatibility test/generator sources are now covered. Shared reader orchestration and tests are covered; encoding byte algorithms, delegated IO/decoder scheduling, binary fixture payloads remain pending. ## Responsibilities and physical identity

The facade publicly owns encoding,format,page_table,reader,writer modules and V1 physical projection helpers. Its documentation declares accepted footer(0,0..=2) and write identity(0,2); the already analyzed exact-version parser maps those identities. The format child forwards metadata only. These files do not select current encoder strategies, commit manifests, publish a Dataset version or implement backend durability. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/mod.rs:1-24) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/format/mod.rs:1-4) (rust/lance-file/src/version.rs:172-272)

|   |-- plain / binary / dictionary: concrete codecs covered separately

The tree follows the public module declarations and dependencies. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/mod.rs:10-23) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:16-33)

## Projection and field mapping

Visit fields in preorder, emitting the parent and then children. Blob and packed-struct fields each occupy one slot and stop recursion, while ordinary struct/container parents also occupy slots even when they have no data page. data_file_columns returns original signed IDs paired with consecutive signed physical indices from0. Counter/count arithmetic is unchecked. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/mod.rs:72-116)

The private BTreeMap casts IDs/indices to u32; repeated IDs retain the final column value. projection_from_field_ids clones the entire supplied schema into an Arc and appends only mapped fields, silently omitting missing mappings. It does not validate empty/repeated/out-of-bounds indices or remove unmatched schema fields. Column-name projection builds the full original mapping before delegating Schema::project, then selects original physical indices. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/mod.rs:25-71) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/mod.rs:93-116)

## Dictionary dispatch and mutation order

read_binary_array accepts exactly Utf8,Binary,LargeUtf8,LargeBinary, converts parameters first and dispatches to the corresponding BinaryDecoder; other types return InvalidInput. read_fixed_stride_array checks the local fixed-stride predicate, returns Schema on false, constructs PlainDecoder, then converts parameters and awaits get. Neither wrapper independently checks offsets or response sizes. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:35-90)

write_schema_dictionaries scans every ID from0 through max_field_id, skipping holes/nondictionaries. Missing dictionary metadata is IO; missing values is InvalidInput. The actual array type chooses numeric PlainEncoder or binary-like BinaryEncoder; unsupported values give Schema. Only successful encode updates offset/length. Earlier writes and mutations survive later errors; no transaction, shutdown or abort is provided. Cost includes sparse ID-span traversal and repeated schema lookup. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:92-132)

Hydration recursively processes nondictionary roots/children in order. For a dictionary it uses the schema value type, reads the entire stored region and replaces values, even when values was already Some. Binary values use nullable=true; only eight signed/unsigned integer types take the fixed-stride branch. It does not recurse below a dictionary node. async_recursion boxes recursion without explicit task spawning; successful earlier fields remain mutated on error/cancellation. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:134-192)

Write and read predicates are asymmetric. The write side asks is_numeric rather than the read side's explicit integer whitelist. The local is_binary_like also accepts Utf8View/BinaryView, which the four-type binary reader rejects. Concrete BinaryEncoder also rejects both view types; PlainEncoder writes fixed-width numeric buffers, while hydration retains its narrower integer whitelist. Complete codec contracts and test limits are now documented separately. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:91-105; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:90-115) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:47-70) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:116-127) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:143-176) (rust/lance-arrow/src/lib.rs:99-142)

The table manifest writer and schema-hydration adapter call these helpers only for ConcreteFileVersion::V1. The complete [V1 writer](rust-lance-file-v1-writer.md) now establishes provider/finish/error ordering: data page table, statistics, dictionaries/provider schema, Metadata and magics, followed by shutdown. (rust/lance-table/src/io/manifest.rs:212-230; rust/lance-table/src/format/manifest.rs:619-631; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:627-651)

## Metadata and logical row grouping

Metadata stores Vec<i32> cumulative batch offsets, usize page-table position, Option manifest position and optional statistics. Empty offsets report0batches/rows; otherwise batches=len-1 and rows=last cast to usize. push_batch_length seeds0 and appends an unchecked signed sum. Negative/zero lengths and malformed sentinel vectors are not rejected. get_offset can access the terminal sentinel; get_batch_length computes next-current with current default0, including the unusual negative-ID boundary. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/format/metadata.rs:14-33) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/format/metadata.rs:85-123)

Protobuf conversion clones offsets and statistics IDs, casts positions unchecked and flattens only statistics fields, dropping schema-level metadata. Missing manifest position encodes0, while decode always yields Some, including Some(0). Wire0 means externally stored manifest; the object converter does not normalize it back to None. Statistics schema decoding can fail; remaining shape/monotonicity/range validation is absent. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/format/metadata.rs:34-78) (protos/file.proto:25-93)

group_indices_to_batches clones and sorts input despite its sorted-input precondition comment. It preserves duplicate indices but loses original order, scans batch ends, groups in ascending batch ID and subtracts start offsets. Out-of-file rows can form terminal batch num_batches; nonempty indices with no offsets panic. range_to_batches unwraps the last offset and checks only end<=length, then binary-searches start cast to i32 and forms clamped subranges. PageInfo holds position and logical length as usize; observed fixed/binary/dictionary writers use the number of array elements, not encoded byte count. PageTable privately owns BTreeMap<i32,BTreeMap<i32,PageInfo>>. set accepts arbitrary signed keys and overwrites; get distinguishes absent None from explicit Some(0,0). For valid dimensions, values count=2*(max-min+1)*num_batches and byte count=16*(max-min+1)*num_batches. No header or dimension vector is written here. write rejects empty outer maps and supplied min above observed minimum as InvalidInput. The builder initially reserves only one element per cell. A loaded zero-batch table panics at the max-batch unwrap; sparse large IDs can amplify memory and bytes. # Frozen V1 foundations: projection, dictionaries, metadata and page tables

Complete local scope: five files / 854 physical lines, including five tests. Concrete binary/plain/dictionary codecs are covered in the [codec supplement](rust-lance-file-v1-codecs.md); the [full V1 reader](rust-lance-file-v1-reader.md) is covered; binary fixtures remain pending. These are historical compatibility surfaces; new capabilities belong in current formats/write paths. Tests were read, not run. (AGENTS.md:7-18)

[Crate](rust-lance-file.md) · [Current composition](rust-lance-file-composition.md) · [V2_0 and compatibility](rust-lance-file-v20-compatibility.md) · [Orientation](../L0-orientation.md) · [Symbols](../L3-symbols/symbol-index.md) · [Contracts](../L3-symbols/behavior-contracts.md) · [Format](../L3-symbols/format-spec.md) · [Scenarios](../L4-crosscutting/scenarios.md)

## Responsibilities and physical identity

The facade publicly owns encoding,format,page_table,reader,writer modules and V1 physical projection helpers. Its documentation declares accepted footer(0,0..=2) and write identity(0,2); the already analyzed exact-version parser maps those identities. The format child forwards metadata only. These files do not select current encoder strategies, commit manifests, publish a Dataset version or implement backend durability. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/mod.rs:1-24) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/format/mod.rs:1-4) (rust/lance-file/src/version.rs:172-272)

~~~text
v1
|-- mod: preorder Field IDs and physical-column projection
|-- encoding: value-codec dispatch and dictionary write/hydration
|   |-- plain / binary / dictionary: concrete codecs covered separately
|-- format/metadata: cumulative batch offsets and protobuf conversion
|-- page_table: sparse map <-> dense field-major pair matrix
+-- reader / writer: full local lifecycle covered in supplements
`-- writer/statistics: full algorithms and test oracles covered in supplement
~~~

The tree follows the public module declarations and dependencies. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/mod.rs:10-23) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:16-33)

## Projection and field mapping

Visit fields in preorder, emitting the parent and then children. Blob and packed-struct fields each occupy one slot and stop recursion, while ordinary struct/container parents also occupy slots even when they have no data page. data_file_columns returns original signed IDs paired with consecutive signed physical indices from0. Counter/count arithmetic is unchecked. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/mod.rs:72-116)

The private BTreeMap casts IDs/indices to u32; repeated IDs retain the final column value. projection_from_field_ids clones the entire supplied schema into an Arc and appends only mapped fields, silently omitting missing mappings. It does not validate empty/repeated/out-of-bounds indices or remove unmatched schema fields. Column-name projection builds the full original mapping before delegating Schema::project, then selects original physical indices. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/mod.rs:25-71) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/mod.rs:93-116)

## Dictionary dispatch and mutation order

read_binary_array accepts exactly Utf8,Binary,LargeUtf8,LargeBinary, converts parameters first and dispatches to the corresponding BinaryDecoder; other types return InvalidInput. read_fixed_stride_array checks the local fixed-stride predicate, returns Schema on false, constructs PlainDecoder, then converts parameters and awaits get. Neither wrapper independently checks offsets or response sizes. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:35-90)

write_schema_dictionaries scans every ID from0 through max_field_id, skipping holes/nondictionaries. Missing dictionary metadata is IO; missing values is InvalidInput. The actual array type chooses numeric PlainEncoder or binary-like BinaryEncoder; unsupported values give Schema. Only successful encode updates offset/length. Earlier writes and mutations survive later errors; no transaction, shutdown or abort is provided. Cost includes sparse ID-span traversal and repeated schema lookup. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:92-132)

Hydration recursively processes nondictionary roots/children in order. For a dictionary it uses the schema value type, reads the entire stored region and replaces values, even when values was already Some. Binary values use nullable=true; only eight signed/unsigned integer types take the fixed-stride branch. It does not recurse below a dictionary node. async_recursion boxes recursion without explicit task spawning; successful earlier fields remain mutated on error/cancellation. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:134-192)

Write and read predicates are asymmetric. The write side asks is_numeric rather than the read side's explicit integer whitelist. The local is_binary_like also accepts Utf8View/BinaryView, which the four-type binary reader rejects. Concrete BinaryEncoder also rejects both view types; PlainEncoder writes fixed-width numeric buffers, while hydration retains its narrower integer whitelist. Complete codec contracts and test limits are now documented separately. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:91-105; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:90-115) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:47-70) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:116-127) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:143-176) (rust/lance-arrow/src/lib.rs:99-142)

The table manifest writer and schema-hydration adapter call these helpers only for ConcreteFileVersion::V1. The complete [V1 writer](rust-lance-file-v1-writer.md) now establishes provider/finish/error ordering: data page table, statistics, dictionaries/provider schema, Metadata and magics, followed by shutdown. (rust/lance-table/src/io/manifest.rs:212-230; rust/lance-table/src/format/manifest.rs:619-631; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:627-651)

## Metadata and logical row grouping

Metadata stores Vec<i32> cumulative batch offsets, usize page-table position, Option manifest position and optional statistics. Empty offsets report0batches/rows; otherwise batches=len-1 and rows=last cast to usize. push_batch_length seeds0 and appends an unchecked signed sum. # Frozen V1 writer, schema provider and finalization

Complete local scope: all 1,311 lines of writer/mod.rs, including seven active tests. The statistics child has contextual dispatch/collector coverage only; its complete algorithms and tests remain pending. These are frozen compatibility paths, not a base for new format capabilities. Tests were read, not run. (AGENTS.md:13-18)

[File crate](rust-lance-file.md) · [L2 writer](../L2-files/rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs.md) · [V1 reader](rust-lance-file-v1-reader.md) · [Codecs](rust-lance-file-v1-codecs.md) · [Foundations](rust-lance-file-v1-foundation.md) · [Symbols](../L3-symbols/symbol-index.md) · [Contracts](../L3-symbols/behavior-contracts.md) · [Scenarios](../L4-crosscutting/scenarios.md)

## Ownership and configuration

FileWriter<M: ManifestProvider + Send + Sync> owns a Box<dyn Writer>, Schema, signed next batch ID, ordinary page table, cumulative metadata and optional statistics collector. Only object_writer is public; the provider is a PhantomData marker, not a runtime instance. The writer has no closed flag, custom Drop, abort guard or ownership-consuming finish. Replacing the public writer does not reset stored state. The ignored example is obsolete: actual calls are try_new, write with a slice, and async finish. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:66-87; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:98-137; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:255-290)

FileWriterOptions has one field: collect_stats_for_fields. None selects every schema ID; Some(empty) disables statistics; nonempty IDs are projected with include_all_children=true before supported fields become collector builders. Unknown IDs are not explicitly rejected here. The collector may return None even after a nonempty request. The contextual support predicate accepts Boolean, signed/unsigned integers, Float32/64, Date32/64, UTF8/Binary with both offset widths and Decimal128; it excludes several types that collect_statistics can independently dispatch, including timestamps, duration, dictionary and fixed binary. Do not equate dispatcher support with automatic collection. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:89-137; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:440-455; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/statistics.rs:550-633)

try_new creates the target object before constructing local state. with_object_writer accepts an arbitrary writer position and supplied schema without validation or dictionary hydration. There is no local environment variable, version selector, compression setting or memory budget. Store creation/overwrite policy and backend cleanup are delegated and still require IO implementation analysis. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:99-137)

## Per-call state transitions

| Stage | Effects and failure boundary |
|---|---|
| Empty input slice | Returns Ok without validation, stats, IO, flush or counter changes |
| Validate every input batch | Convert Arrow schema; compare with stored schema ignoring declared nullability, metadata, field IDs and dictionary contents; recursively reject actual nulls in stored nonnullable fields |
| Collect stats | One row per supported selected field for the entire slice; mutates builders before writes |
| Write roots sequentially | Clone schema fields, find batch columns by name, recursively encode all arrays at current batch ID; earlier page entries and bytes survive later failure |
| Append logical length | Unchecked i32 row casts/sum and cumulative offset mutation |
| Flush | Polls in-flight writer requests before caller regains control; a failure leaves cumulative metadata advanced |
| Advance batch ID | Happens only after successful flush |

Evidence: rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:166-236. A single call with several batches creates one stored batch. A nonempty slice containing a zero-row batch still traverses encoding and advances the batch ID on success; it is not the empty-slice no-op. The zero-row UTF8 test explicitly reopens batch0. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:985-1014)

Schema comparison retains normal ordered name/logical-type/child matching, with the shared blob-child comparison exception inherited from Field. Recursive nullability checks zip field children with ArrayData child_data and inspect physical null counts without ancestor masks or list-child logical-span slicing. They do not independently validate counts; normal schema comparison occurs first. Dictionary equality is assumed by a comment to have been checked earlier, but this writer performs no comparison or unification. (rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/field.rs:83-103; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/field.rs:423-440; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:930-980; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:144-199)
